f: 444. Why does "fasting a day" (siyam yawman) require waiting until sunset?
b: Because when combined with an act of duration, "day" refers to the complete daylight period.

f: 445. If a husband says, "If you bear a boy you are divorced once, and if you bear a girl you are divorced twice," and the woman gives birth to both at the same time, how many divorces are legally enforced?
b: Only one divorce is enforced by the court.

f: 446. Why does only one divorce apply when twins of different genders are born and their order is unknown?
b: Because the court cannot establish which condition occurred first.

f: 447. What is recommended regarding the number of divorces when twins of different genders are born under a conditional divorce oath?
b: It is recommended as a precaution to act as though two divorces occurred.

f: 448. When does the waiting period (iddah) end in the case of a pregnant woman giving birth to twins?
b: It ends with the birth.

f: 449. If a husband says, "If you speak to A and B, you are divorced three times," and the two conditions occur during different periods of marriage, does the oath remain active?
b: Yes, according to the Hanafi school, as long as the legal capacity (dhimmah) remains.

f: 450. According to the Hanafi school, why can a multi-part divorce condition remain active through different marriage periods?
b: Because the obligation continues as long as the person remains legally capable of fulfilling the condition.

f: 451. If one part of a divorce condition occurs before marriage and another part occurs while the marriage exists, when does divorce occur?
b: Divorce occurs when the remaining condition is fulfilled while the marriage is active.

f: 452. According to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, what happens to previous divorces if a divorced woman marries another man and later returns to her first husband?
b: The previous divorces are erased, and the husband receives a new quota of three divorces.

f: 453. Why do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ consider a second marriage destructive of previous divorce counts?
b: Because the intervening marriage removes the effect of the earlier divorce count.

f: 454. According to Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Zufar, what happens to previous divorces if a woman returns to her first husband after another marriage?
b: The previous divorces remain, and only the remaining quota is available.

f: 455. According to Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Zufar, if a husband had divorced his wife twice before her second marriage, how many divorces remain when she returns?
b: One divorce remains.

f: 456. If a husband makes a conditional oath for three divorces and then issues three unconditional divorces, what happens to the conditional oath?
b: It becomes exhausted and void.

f: 457. Why does a three-divorce conditional oath become exhausted after three unconditional divorces?
b: Because the full legal capacity of three divorces has already been consumed.

f: 458. If a woman marries another man and returns after three divorces have already occurred, can the previous conditional divorce oath activate again?
b: No.

f: 459. Why can a previously exhausted three-divorce oath not reactivate after remarriage?
b: Because there are no remaining divorces available under that oath.

f: 460. If a husband makes a conditional oath for three divorces and then issues an unconditional divorce that ends the marriage, what happens to the conditional oath?
b: The conditional oath is considered exhausted.

f: 461. Why is a conditional divorce oath exhausted after the marriage ends through an unconditional divorce?
b: Because the marriage bond, which is the place (mahall) where the divorce would take effect, no longer exists.

f: 462. Can a conditional divorce oath be revived if the husband remarries the same woman after the marriage ended?
b: No.

f: 463. Why can a conditional divorce oath not be revived after remarriage?
b: Because the oath was already exhausted when the original marriage ended.

f: 464. If a husband says, "If I have intercourse with you, you are divorced three times," when does the divorce occur?
b: The divorce occurs at the moment penetration occurs.

f: 465. What physical act triggers divorce in the statement "If I have intercourse with you, you are divorced three times"?
b: The meeting of the circumcised parts (taqi al-khitanan), meaning penetration.

f: 466. If a husband remains inside after the conditional divorce is triggered, is an additional mahr owed?
b: No.

f: 467. Why is no additional mahr owed if the husband remains inside after conditional divorce is triggered?
b: Because it is considered one continuous act of intercourse.

f: 468. If a husband withdraws and then re-enters after conditional divorce has occurred, is another mahr owed?
b: Yes.

f: 469. Why does withdrawal and re-entry create an obligation of mahr after conditional divorce?
b: Because it is considered a new act of intercourse after the marriage bond has ended.

f: 470. What compensation is owed for intercourse after divorce in this situation?
b: The compensation known as 'aqr.

f: 471. What is Abu Yusuf's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ view regarding intercourse continuing after conditional divorce?
b: He considers continued intercourse without withdrawal sufficient to create a new obligation of mahr.

f: 472. Why do scholars agree that legal punishment (hadd) does not apply in this situation?
b: Because there is ambiguity due to the possibility that the act is considered a continuation of the original intercourse.

f: 473. If a husband says, "You are divorced, if God wills" (in sha' Allah) in one continuous statement, does divorce occur?
b: No.

f: 474. Why does saying "if God wills" immediately after a divorce statement prevent the divorce from occurring?
b: Because the exception (istithna') acts as a conditional modifier that prevents the oath from taking effect.

f: 475. What is the condition required for the phrase "if God wills" to cancel a divorce statement?
b: It must be connected continuously in the same breath or statement.

f: 476. If a husband says "You are divorced" and pauses before adding "if God wills," does the exception cancel the divorce?
b: No.

f: 477. Why does adding "if God wills" after a pause not cancel the divorce?
b: Because the divorce has already taken effect, and the later condition is treated as an invalid retraction.

f: 478. What is the ruling if a husband says "Three except one" regarding divorce?
b: Two divorces occur.

f: 479. What is the ruling if a husband says "Three except two" regarding divorce?
b: One divorce occurs.

f: 480. What is the ruling if a husband says "Three except three" regarding divorce?
b: Three divorces occur.

f: 481. Why does "Three except three" still result in three divorces rather than zero?
b: Because removing the entire number leaves no original statement for the exception to modify, so the exception fails.

f: 482. According to the Hanafi interpretation, what function does an exception (istithna') serve in numerical divorce statements?
b: It specifies the final numerical result.

f: 483. Is it linguistically valid to state a complete number and subtract part of it in a divorce statement?
b: Yes.

f: 484. Why is "Three except one" considered valid in divorce wording?
b: Because stating the total and subtracting a portion is an accepted linguistic method of specification.

f: 485. If a man divorces his wife during his terminal illness with an irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bāʾin) and dies while she is still in her waiting period (ʿiddah), does she inherit from him according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes. According to the Ḥanafīs, she inherits from him if he dies while she is still in her waiting period, because the marital relationship is considered to remain existent regarding certain legal effects, including inheritance.

f: 486. If a man divorces his wife during his terminal illness with an irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bāʾin) and dies after her waiting period (ʿiddah) has ended, does she inherit from him according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No. Once the waiting period has ended, she does not inherit from him because there is no longer any possibility of considering the marriage bond existent, and the marital relationship is no longer a cause for inheritance.

f: 487. What was Al-Shāfiʿī’s position regarding a woman divorced during her husband's terminal illness inheriting from him?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī held that she does not inherit from him in either case, whether he dies during her waiting period or after it, because the marital bond was terminated by the divorce.

f: 488. What was Al-Shāfiʿī’s reasoning for denying inheritance to a woman divorced during her husband's terminal illness?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī argued that the marital bond is the cause of inheritance, and since the divorce terminated that bond, she cannot inherit. He also reasoned that if she dies after such a divorce, the husband would not inherit from her either.

f: 489. Why does the Ḥanafī school allow a woman divorced during her husband's terminal illness to inherit from him?
b: The Ḥanafīs argue that the marital relationship is the cause of her inheritance, and the husband intended to remove her inheritance right through the divorce. Therefore, his intention is rejected by delaying the effect of the divorce regarding inheritance until the completion of her waiting period, preventing harm from reaching her.

f: 490. Why is delaying the effect of the divorce regarding inheritance possible during the waiting period?
b: It is possible because the marriage during the waiting period remains existent with respect to some legal effects. Therefore, it can also be considered existent regarding her inheritance from him.

f: 491. Why does a divorced woman not inherit from her husband after completing her waiting period?
b: After the completion of the waiting period, there is no longer any possibility of considering the marriage bond existent. Therefore, the marital relationship is no longer a cause for inheritance.

f: 492. If a man divorces his wife three times at her request and then dies while she is in her waiting period, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit from him because she accepted the cancellation of her own inheritance right.

f: 493. If a wife asks her husband to divorce her three times and he does so, why does she lose her right of inheritance if he dies during her waiting period?
b: Because she accepted the cancellation of her own right, and the delaying of the divorce's effect was originally intended to protect her from harm, not to benefit someone who willingly accepted the loss of that right.

f: 494. If a husband tells his wife "Choose" and she chooses herself, then he dies during her waiting period, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit from him because by choosing herself she accepted the cancellation of her inheritance right.

f: 495. If a wife performs khulʿ with her husband and he dies while she is in her waiting period, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because she accepted the removal of the marital relationship and thereby accepted the cancellation of her inheritance right.

f: 496. If a wife says to her husband "Divorce me with a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī)" and he divorces her three times, does she inherit from him if he dies during her waiting period?
b: Yes. She inherits from him because a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) does not remove the marriage bond, and by requesting it she did not consent to losing her inheritance right.

f: 497. Why does a woman who requested a revocable divorce still inherit from her husband if he dies during her waiting period?
b: Because a revocable divorce does not terminate the marital bond. Therefore, her request was not an acceptance of the loss of her inheritance right.

f: 498. If a man during his terminal illness says to his wife, "I divorced you three times while I was healthy and your waiting period has already ended," and she confirms it, then he later acknowledges a debt owed to her or makes a bequest for her, what is her entitlement according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, she receives the lesser of two amounts: either the amount of the debt/bequest or her inheritance share.

f: 499. What was the position of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad regarding a husband's acknowledgment of a debt or bequest for his wife after he claimed he divorced her while healthy and her waiting period ended?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad held that his acknowledgment of the debt and his bequest are valid.

f: 500. If a man divorces his wife three times during his terminal illness at her request, and then acknowledges a debt owed to her or makes a bequest for her, what is the ruling according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Muḥammad?
b: According to all three imams, she receives the lesser of the acknowledged amount/bequest and her inheritance share.

f: 501. What was Zufar’s opinion regarding a man who divorces his wife three times during his terminal illness at her request and then acknowledges a debt or makes a bequest for her?
b: Zufar held that she receives everything he bequeathed and everything he acknowledged as a debt.

f: 502. Why did Zufar consider the husband's acknowledgment and bequest valid when the wife requested divorce during his terminal illness?
b: Zufar reasoned that since her inheritance was already invalidated due to her request for divorce, the obstacle preventing the validity of the acknowledgment and bequest was removed.

f: 503. Why did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad consider the acknowledgment and bequest valid in the first case where the husband claimed he divorced her while healthy?
b: They reasoned that since both parties agreed that the divorce occurred and the waiting period had ended, she became a non-wife to him. Therefore, it became permissible for him to marry her sister, removing the suspicion that he intended to increase her inheritance through the acknowledgment or bequest.

f: 504. How does the completion of the waiting period remove suspicion according to Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: Once the waiting period ends, the marital relationship is fully terminated, so there is no longer suspicion that the husband is using an acknowledgment or bequest to give his wife additional wealth beyond her inheritance.

f: 505. What examples did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad use to show that the woman in the first case is treated as a stranger to the husband?
b: They mentioned that his testimony for her is accepted and that it is permissible to give zakāh to her, unlike the case where the waiting period has not ended.

f: 506. Why is zakāh permissible to give to the woman in the first case but not a basis for suspicion?
b: Because there is no remaining marital relationship or customary suspicion of collusion between them after the waiting period has ended.

f: 507. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ maintain that suspicion remains in both cases?
b: Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ argues that the woman may request divorce in order to allow the husband to acknowledge a debt or make a bequest for her, thereby increasing what she receives beyond her inheritance share.

f: 508. What type of arrangement did Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ fear could occur between a husband and wife in these cases?
b: He feared that the husband and wife could agree to falsely acknowledge separation and completion of the waiting period so that he could give her more wealth than she would receive through inheritance.

f: 509. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ reject the increase beyond the inheritance share but allow the inheritance share itself?
b: He rejects the increase because of the suspicion of collusion, but there is no suspicion regarding the inheritance amount itself because it is her established legal right.

f: 510. Why is there no suspicion regarding zakāh, marriage, and testimony according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Because there is no customary practice of collusion in these matters. Therefore, these rulings are not affected by the same suspicion that exists regarding increasing a woman's inheritance through acknowledgments and bequests.

f: 511. According to Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad, what is the main factor determining whether suspicion exists in these inheritance-related cases?
b: The existence or absence of the waiting period is the main factor. If the waiting period remains, suspicion exists; if it has ended, suspicion is removed.

f: 512. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, what principle determines rulings in cases involving possible collusion between spouses?
b: The ruling is based on the presence of suspicion, and matters involving marriage and kinship are considered when determining whether such suspicion exists.

f: 513. If a man who is prevented from reaching his wife or is in the ranks of battle divorces his wife three times and then dies, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit from him because the ruling of a person fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance is not established in these cases, as death is not generally expected.

f: 514. If a man fighting in single combat divorces his wife three times and is then killed, does she inherit from him?
b: Yes. She inherits from him because the likelihood of death is present, so the ruling of a person fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance applies.

f: 515. If a man is brought forward to be killed by qiṣāṣ (retaliation) or rajm (stoning) and divorces his wife three times, does she inherit from him if he dies?
b: Yes. She inherits because his situation carries a prevailing expectation of death, so the ruling of fleeing is established.

f: 516. What is the basis for allowing the wife of a person fleeing from depriving her of inheritance to inherit from him?
b: The basis is istiḥsān (juristic preference), which gives her inheritance because the husband intended to remove her inheritance right through divorce.

f: 517. When is the ruling of a person fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance established?
b: It is established when the wife's right becomes attached to the husband's wealth, which occurs during an illness in which death is generally feared.

f: 518. What type of illness causes the ruling of a person fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance to apply?
b: It applies to an illness in which death is generally feared, such as when a person becomes confined to his bed and cannot carry out his normal activities like a healthy person.

f: 519. Why is a person confined in a fortress not treated like someone fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance?
b: Because the prevailing expectation is safety, as the fortress protects him from the enemy. Therefore, the likelihood of death is not established.

f: 520. Why is a person in the ranks of battle not treated like someone fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance?
b: Because military strength and the presence of soldiers provide protection, making safety the prevailing expectation rather than death.

f: 521. Why is a person fighting in single combat treated like someone fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance?
b: Because in single combat the prevailing expectation is death, so the condition of fearing death is present.

f: 522. Does it matter whether a person in a situation of expected death dies from that specific cause or from another cause?
b: No. If he dies while in that condition, the same ruling applies regardless of whether the death occurs from that particular cause or another cause.

f: 523. What evidence shows that the cause of death does not affect the ruling in cases of expected death?
b: The statement "if he dies in that situation or is killed" indicates that there is no difference between dying from that cause or another cause, similar to a person confined to bed due to illness who dies while in that state.

f: 524. If a healthy man says to his wife, "When the beginning of the month comes, you are divorced," and the beginning of the month occurs while he is sick, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because the conditional divorce statement was made while he was healthy, before her inheritance right became attached to his wealth.

f: 525. If a healthy man says, "If you enter the house, you are divorced," and she enters the house while he is sick, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because the conditional statement was made while he was healthy.

f: 526. If a healthy man says, "If so-and-so prays the ẓuhr prayer, you are divorced," and that person prays while the husband is sick, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because the divorce condition was set while he was healthy.

f: 527. If a sick man says, "When the beginning of the month comes, you are divorced," and the beginning of the month occurs while he is sick, does she inherit from him?
b: Yes. She inherits because he made the conditional divorce statement while his illness existed and her inheritance right was already attached to his wealth.

f: 528. If a sick man says, "If so-and-so enters the house," or "If so-and-so prays the ẓuhr prayer," and the condition occurs while he is sick, does she inherit from him?
b: Yes. She inherits because the conditional divorce was created during the illness in which death was feared.

f: 529. What are the four categories of conditional divorce statements mentioned in this discussion?
b: They are: attaching divorce to the arrival of a time, attaching divorce to the action of another person, attaching divorce to the husband's own action, and attaching divorce to the wife's action.

f: 530. What are the two possible situations regarding a conditional divorce statement made during illness?
b: Either the statement was made while the husband was healthy and the condition occurred while he was sick, or both the statement and the condition occurred while he was sick.

f: 531. Why does a wife inherit when both the conditional divorce statement and its condition occur during the husband's illness?
b: Because the husband's intention of fleeing from her inheritance right is realized by him creating the conditional divorce while her right was already attached to his wealth.

f: 532. Why does a wife not inherit when the conditional divorce statement was made while the husband was healthy and the condition occurred while he was sick?
b: Because the conditional divorce was established before the illness in which her inheritance right became attached to his wealth, so the ruling of fleeing does not apply.

f: 533. Is there an exception among conditional divorce statements made during illness?
b: Yes. The statement "If you enter the house, you are divorced" has a special ruling mentioned in the text.

f: 534. What is the special ruling for the statement "If you enter the house, you are divorced" when the husband makes it while sick?
b: Unlike other conditional statements, this statement does not result in inheritance for the wife according to the text.

f: 535. What was Zufar's opinion regarding a conditional divorce made before illness that takes effect when the condition occurs during illness?
b: Zufar held that the wife inherits because a divorce suspended upon a condition becomes effective when the condition occurs, making it equivalent to a divorce issued during illness.

f: 536. What is the Ḥanafī response to Zufar's argument that a conditional divorce occurring during illness is like an immediate divorce during illness?
b: The Ḥanafīs argue that the earlier conditional statement only becomes a divorce due to the legal occurrence of the condition, not because of the husband's intention at that time. Since injustice occurs through intention, his action is not rejected.

f: 537. When a husband attaches divorce to his own action, is he considered someone fleeing from depriving his wife of inheritance?
b: Yes. Whether the conditional statement was made while he was healthy and the condition occurs during illness, or both occurred during illness, he is considered someone fleeing.

f: 538. Why is a husband considered fleeing when he attaches divorce to his own action?
b: Because the intention of removing his wife's inheritance right exists either when he makes the conditional statement or when he performs the condition during his illness.

f: 539. If a husband has no alternative but to perform the action upon which he suspended the divorce, is he still considered fleeing?
b: Yes. Even if he cannot avoid performing the action, he had the choice to make the conditional statement in the first place, so his action is rejected to prevent harm from reaching his wife.

f: 540. If a husband suspends divorce upon his wife's action, what are the rulings depending on whether she has a choice in performing that action?
b: If the action is voluntary and she chooses to do it, she does not inherit because she consented. If the action is unavoidable and she is compelled to do it, she inherits because there is no consent under compulsion.

f: 541. If a sick husband says, "If you speak to Zayd, you are divorced," and she chooses to speak to Zayd, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because speaking to Zayd is an action she could choose to avoid, so her action indicates consent.

f: 542. If a sick husband says, "If you eat food," "if you pray ẓuhr," or "if you speak with your parents," you are divorced, and she performs the action, does she inherit from him?
b: Yes. She inherits because these are necessary actions she cannot avoid without harm in this world or the Hereafter, so her action is considered compelled rather than voluntary.

f: 543. Why does compulsion remove the wife's consent in conditional divorce cases?
b: Because there is no genuine consent when a person is forced to perform an action and cannot avoid it due to harm.

f: 544. If the husband made a conditional divorce statement while healthy and his wife's voluntary action occurs during his illness, does she inherit?
b: No. She does not inherit because the action was something she chose, and the conditional statement was made before her inheritance right became attached to his wealth.

f: 545. If the husband made a conditional divorce statement while healthy and his wife's unavoidable action occurs during his illness, what was Muḥammad's opinion?
b: According to Muḥammad, she does not inherit because the husband did not perform any action after her inheritance right became attached to his wealth.

f: 546. What was Zufar's opinion regarding a wife's unavoidable action when the conditional divorce statement was made while the husband was healthy?
b: Zufar agreed with Muḥammad that she does not inherit because nothing was done by the husband after her right became attached to his wealth.

f: 547. What was the opinion of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding a wife's unavoidable action when the conditional divorce statement was made while the husband was healthy?
b: They held that she inherits because the husband effectively forced her into performing the action, so the action is attributed back to him.

f: 548. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ attribute the wife's unavoidable action back to the husband?
b: Because she was like a tool in his hand, similar to a person acting under coercion, so the husband's action is considered the true cause.

f: 549. What are the four categories of conditional divorce mentioned in this discussion and their general rulings?
b: (1) Divorce attached to time: generally follows whether the statement was made before or during illness. (2) Divorce attached to another person's action: similar to time. (3) Divorce attached to the husband's own action: he is considered fleeing and the wife inherits. (4) Divorce attached to the wife's action: inheritance depends on whether her action was voluntary or compelled.

f: 550. If a man divorces his wife three times while he is sick, then recovers and later dies, does she inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because recovery removes the terminal illness (marad al-mawt), making the previous illness equivalent to health. It becomes clear that her inheritance right was never attached to his wealth, and he is not considered someone fleeing from depriving her of inheritance.

f: 551. What was Zufar's opinion regarding a man who divorces his wife three times while sick, recovers, and later dies?
b: Zufar held that she inherits because the husband intended to deprive her of inheritance when he divorced her during illness, and he died while she was still in her waiting period.

f: 552. Why do the majority of Ḥanafīs reject Zufar's opinion regarding divorce during illness followed by recovery?
b: They argue that recovery removes the ruling of terminal illness. Since the illness ended, it is as though the husband was healthy, so the wife never acquired a right connected to his wealth during a terminal illness.

f: 553. If a man divorces his wife three times, then she apostatizes, returns to Islam, and he dies from his illness while she is still in her waiting period, does she inherit?
b: No. She does not inherit because apostasy removed her eligibility for inheritance. An apostate cannot inherit, and inheritance cannot continue without legal eligibility.

f: 554. If a woman divorced three times does not apostatize but willingly allows her husband's son to have intercourse with her, does she inherit from her former husband if he dies during her waiting period?
b: Yes. She inherits because this act does not remove her eligibility for inheritance. The prohibition caused by this act does not contradict inheritance, so her eligibility remains.

f: 555. Why does apostasy prevent a divorced woman from inheriting while allowing intercourse with her husband's son does not?
b: Apostasy removes the person's legal eligibility for inheritance, whereas the prohibition caused by intercourse with the husband's son does not remove inheritance eligibility.

f: 556. Why is willingly allowing intercourse with the husband's son different when the marriage still exists?
b: When the marriage still exists, such an act establishes separation, so she is considered to have consented to removing the cause of inheritance (the marriage). After three divorces, however, the three divorces already preceded the act, so the situation is different.

f: 557. If a husband accuses his wife of adultery while he is healthy and performs liʿān during his illness, does she inherit from him according to the majority of the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, she inherits because she was forced to pursue liʿān proceedings to remove the accusation and disgrace from herself.

f: 558. What was Muḥammad's opinion regarding a husband who accuses his wife of adultery while healthy and performs liʿān during illness?
b: Muḥammad held that she does not inherit.

f: 559. If the accusation of adultery and the liʿān both occur during the husband's illness, does the wife inherit according to all three Ḥanafī imams?
b: Yes. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Muḥammad, she inherits because the accusation occurred during the illness in which her inheritance right was attached to his wealth.

f: 560. Why is liʿān compared to a conditional divorce attached to the wife's unavoidable action?
b: Because the wife is forced to pursue legal proceedings to remove the accusation of adultery and protect her honor, so her action is not considered voluntary consent.

f: 561. If a man makes an oath of īlāʾ (abstention from intercourse) while healthy and separation occurs through īlāʾ while he is sick, does his wife inherit from him?
b: No. She does not inherit because the īlāʾ was established while he was healthy.

f: 562. If a man makes an oath of īlāʾ while sick and separation occurs through īlāʾ during his illness, does his wife inherit?
b: Yes. She inherits because the īlāʾ was initiated during the illness in which her inheritance right became attached to his wealth.

f: 563. Why is īlāʾ treated like a conditional divorce attached to the arrival of a time?
b: Because īlāʾ causes separation after the passing of four months without intercourse, so it is similar to attaching divorce to the occurrence of a time-based condition.

f: 564. Does a wife inherit after a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) if her husband dies during her waiting period?
b: Yes. She inherits in all situations because revocable divorce does not remove the marriage bond, so the cause of inheritance remains present.

f: 565. Why does a woman divorced through revocable divorce continue to inherit from her husband?
b: Because the marriage is not fully terminated by revocable divorce until the waiting period ends or the divorce becomes final, so the legal cause of inheritance remains.

f: 566. In all the cases where a divorced woman inherits from her husband, what condition must be fulfilled?
b: She only inherits if the husband dies while she is still in her waiting period (ʿiddah).

f: 567. Does a divorced woman inherit from her husband if he dies after her waiting period has ended?
b: No. Once the waiting period ends, the marital relationship is no longer present and she no longer has a right of inheritance.

f: 568. After a man divorces his wife with one or two revocable divorces (ṭalāq rajʿī), does he have the right to take her back during her waiting period?
b: Yes. He has the right to take her back during her waiting period, whether she agrees or refuses.

f: 569. What is the evidence that a husband may take back his wife after a revocable divorce without her consent?
b: The evidence is the verse: "Then retain them in a fair manner" (Qur'an 2:231), which does not distinguish between whether she agrees or not.

f: 570. Why is the continuation of the waiting period necessary for rajʿah to be valid?
b: Because rajʿah is the continuation of the marital bond. This continuation only exists during the waiting period, as after it ends there is no remaining marital ownership.

f: 571. Why did Allah describe taking back a divorced wife as "holding" (imsāk)?
b: Because imsāk means preservation and keeping, indicating that rajʿah is a continuation of the existing marital relationship rather than the creation of a new one.

f: 572. When does the husband lose the right of rajʿah after a revocable divorce?
b: He loses the right when the wife's waiting period ends because the marital bond is no longer considered existent.

f: 573. What are the explicit words that establish rajʿah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Saying: "I have taken you back" or "I have taken my wife back." These are explicit statements of returning to the marriage.

f: 574. Is there any disagreement among the imams regarding rajʿah being valid through explicit words such as "I have taken you back"?
b: No. There is no disagreement among the imams regarding the validity of rajʿah through explicit verbal statements.

f: 575. According to the Ḥanafīs, can rajʿah occur through actions as well as words?
b: Yes. Rajʿah can occur through actions such as intercourse, kissing, touching with desire, or looking at the wife's private part with desire.

f: 576. What was Al-Shāfiʿī’s position regarding rajʿah through actions?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī held that rajʿah is only valid through speech when the husband is capable of speaking, because he considered rajʿah similar to initiating a new marriage.

f: 577. Why did Al-Shāfiʿī consider intercourse with the divorced wife invalid before verbal rajʿah?
b: He considered the divorced wife like a woman outside the marriage until rajʿah is verbally established, making intercourse before that impermissible.

f: 578. What is the Ḥanafī response to Al-Shāfiʿī’s view that rajʿah requires speech?
b: The Ḥanafīs argue that rajʿah is a continuation of the existing marriage, not the establishment of a new marriage. Therefore, actions can indicate continuation of the marriage.

f: 579. What is the analogy used by the Ḥanafīs to prove that actions can establish rajʿah?
b: They compare it to cancelling an option (khiyār), where an action can indicate continuation and acceptance.

f: 580. Why do intercourse, kissing, touching with desire, and looking at the private part with desire indicate rajʿah?
b: Because these actions are specific to marriage, especially regarding a free woman, and therefore indicate continuation of the marital relationship.

f: 581. Why are touching and looking without desire not considered rajʿah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because such actions may occur outside marriage, such as in the case of a doctor, midwife, or similar situations.

f: 582. Why is looking at parts of the body other than the private part not considered rajʿah?
b: Because such looking may occur between people who live together, and the husband and wife are still living together during the waiting period.

f: 583. Why would considering ordinary looking as rajʿah create difficulty?
b: Because the husband would then be forced to divorce her again if he did not intend rajʿah, causing her waiting period to be unnecessarily prolonged.

f: 584. Is it recommended for a husband to have witnesses testify to his rajʿah?
b: Yes. It is recommended that he have two witnesses testify regarding his taking back his wife.

f: 585. If a husband takes back his wife without witnesses, is the rajʿah valid according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes. The rajʿah is valid even without witnesses, although having witnesses is recommended.

f: 586. What was Al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding the requirement of witnesses for rajʿah?
b: In one of his two opinions, Al-Shāfiʿī held that rajʿah is not valid without witnesses.

f: 587. Which other scholar held that witnesses are required for the validity of rajʿah?
b: Mālik held that witnesses are required for the validity of rajʿah.

f: 588. What evidence did those who require witnesses for rajʿah use?
b: They used the verse: "And bring two just witnesses from among you" (Qur'an 65:2), arguing that the command indicates obligation.

f: 589. How do the Ḥanafīs respond to the evidence that witnesses are obligatory for rajʿah?
b: They argue that the texts regarding rajʿah are unrestricted and do not make witnessing a condition for its validity.

f: 590. Why do the Ḥanafīs say witnessing is not a condition for rajʿah?
b: Because rajʿah is a continuation of an existing marriage, and witnessing is not a condition for the continuation of marriage, just as it is not required when a husband returns to his wife after īlāʾ.

f: 591. Why is witnessing recommended for rajʿah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: It is recommended as a precaution to prevent denial and disputes regarding whether rajʿah occurred.

f: 592. How do the Ḥanafīs understand the verse "And bring two just witnesses from among you" regarding rajʿah?
b: They understand it as a recommendation rather than an obligation, because Allah mentioned witnessing together with separation, and witnessing at separation is also recommended rather than obligatory.

f: 593. Why is it recommended for a husband to inform his wife of the rajʿah?
b: So that she does not mistakenly consider herself divorced and commit a sin by acting as though she is no longer married.

f: 594. If the waiting period ends and the husband claims, "I took you back during the waiting period," and the wife confirms this, is the rajʿah valid?
b: Yes. The rajʿah is valid because her confirmation removes the uncertainty surrounding his claim.

f: 595. If the waiting period ends and the husband claims, "I took you back during the waiting period," but the wife denies it, whose statement is accepted?
b: The wife's statement is accepted.

f: 596. Why is the wife's statement accepted when she denies the husband's claim of rajʿah after the waiting period?
b: Because the husband is reporting an event that he no longer has the ability to establish at the present time, making him subject to suspicion.

f: 597. Why does the wife's confirmation validate the husband's claim of rajʿah after the waiting period?
b: Because her confirmation removes the suspicion surrounding his claim.

f: 598. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, is the wife required to swear an oath when she denies the husband's claim of rajʿah?
b: No. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, she is not required to swear an oath.

f: 599. What issue does the discussion of requiring an oath in a wife's denial of rajʿah relate to?
b: It relates to the issue of requiring an oath in the six disputed matters discussed previously in the Book of Marriage.

f: 600. If a husband says, "I have taken you back," and the wife replies, "My waiting period has already ended," is the rajʿah valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: No. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the rajʿah is not valid because the waiting period had already ended according to her statement.

f: 601. What was the opinion of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad regarding a husband claiming rajʿah when the wife says her waiting period ended?
b: They held that the rajʿah is valid because it occurred during the waiting period, which is considered to remain outwardly until she informs him otherwise.

f: 602. Why did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad consider the rajʿah valid in this case?
b: Because the husband's rajʿah occurred before her statement that the waiting period had ended, and the waiting period is treated as continuing outwardly until she informs him.

f: 603. If a husband says to his wife, "I divorced you," and she replies, "My waiting period has already ended," does the divorce occur?
b: Yes. The divorce occurs because the husband’s statement is accepted and the waiting period is considered to remain outwardly until she informs him of its completion.

f: 604. What principle explains why a husband's statement of rajʿah and divorce are treated differently from a wife's statement about the end of her waiting period?
b: The waiting period is considered outwardly continuing until the wife informs him that it has ended, so actions occurring before that information are judged according to the apparent state.

f: 605. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, if a husband claims he took his wife back after the waiting period ended and she confirms the rajʿah, when did the rajʿah actually occur?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the rajʿah occurred after the waiting period had ended, because the wife is trusted regarding informing about the completion of her waiting period.

f: 606. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ consider the rajʿah to have occurred after the waiting period ended if the wife informs him that it ended?
b: Because her statement indicates that the completion of the waiting period preceded his claim of rajʿah, and the closest possible time for its completion is considered to be when he made the statement.

f: 607. Why can a husband’s claimed rajʿah after the waiting period not be accepted according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Because rajʿah can only occur during the waiting period, and his statement comes after the time in which rajʿah was possible.

f: 608. Is the disagreement regarding the timing of rajʿah also present in the issue of divorce?
b: Yes. The same disagreement applies regarding whether a divorce statement is affected by the wife's claim that her waiting period ended.

f: 609. Why does divorce occur even if the wife's waiting period had ended according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Because the husband’s admission itself establishes the divorce after the waiting period, whereas rajʿah cannot be established after the waiting period has ended.

f: 610. If the husband of a slave woman claims after her waiting period ended that he took her back, the master confirms him, and the slave woman denies him, whose statement is accepted according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the statement of the slave woman is accepted.

f: 611. If the husband of a slave woman claims after her waiting period ended that he took her back, and the master and slave woman disagree, whose statement do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad accept?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad accept the statement of the master.

f: 612. Why do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad accept the master's statement regarding rajʿah of a slave woman?
b: Because the slave woman's private part is owned by the master, so the husband is acknowledging something connected to the master's exclusive right, similar to acknowledging that she is married to him.

f: 613. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ reject the master's statement in the first case involving the slave woman?
b: Because rajʿah is based upon the existence of the waiting period, and the statement regarding the waiting period belongs to the woman herself. Therefore, what depends upon the waiting period follows her statement.

f: 614. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who is trusted regarding the end of the waiting period?
b: The woman is trusted regarding the end of her waiting period because she is the one who knows its details.

f: 615. If the situation regarding the slave woman is reversed, whose statement is accepted according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Muḥammad?
b: If the situation is reversed, all three accept the statement of the master.

f: 616. Why is the master's statement accepted in the reversed case involving a slave woman?
b: Because the waiting period has already ended, the master's ownership of enjoyment has become apparent, and the woman's statement cannot remove an established right.

f: 617. Why is the reversed case different from the first case involving the slave woman?
b: In the first case, accepting the master's statement would acknowledge the continuation of the waiting period according to the woman, while the master's ownership does not become apparent until after the waiting period remains established.

f: 618. If a slave woman says, "My waiting period has ended," while both the husband and master say, "Your waiting period has not ended," whose statement is accepted?
b: Her statement is accepted because she is trusted regarding the matter of her waiting period.

f: 619. Why is a woman trusted regarding the completion of her waiting period?
b: Because she is the one who knows her menstruation and waiting period, making her statement authoritative in this matter.

f: 620. After the third menstruation ends, when does the husband's right of rajʿah end according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: If the blood stops after the third menstruation and ten days have passed, the right of rajʿah ends immediately, even if she has not performed ghusl.

f: 621. If menstrual blood stops before ten days after the third menstruation, does the husband's right of rajʿah end immediately?
b: No. His right of rajʿah remains until she performs ghusl or a complete prayer time passes over her.

f: 622. Why does the right of rajʿah end immediately when menstrual blood stops after ten days following the third menstruation?
b: Because menstruation cannot exceed ten days. Therefore, the cessation of blood confirms that menstruation has ended, the waiting period is complete, and rajʿah is no longer possible.

f: 623. Why does the right of rajʿah not end immediately when blood stops before ten days?
b: Because there remains a possibility that the menstrual blood may return, so the cessation alone is not sufficient to establish purity.

f: 624. What two things strengthen the indication of purity when menstrual blood stops before ten days?
b: Either performing ghusl or the passing of a complete prayer time, which establishes a ruling connected to the state of purity.

f: 625. Why is ghusl or the passing of a prayer time required when menstrual blood stops before ten days?
b: Because these actions confirm that the woman has entered the state of purity, removing the uncertainty that the blood may return.

f: 626. Does the same waiting-period rule apply to a woman from the People of the Book?
b: No. For a woman from the People of the Book, mere cessation of blood is sufficient because the possibility of another confirming sign is not expected from her.

f: 627. Why is mere cessation of blood sufficient for a woman from the People of the Book?
b: Because the additional sign of purification through ghusl is not expected from her, so the uncertainty is treated differently.

f: 628. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, when does the right of rajʿah end if a woman performs tayammum and prays?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the right of rajʿah ends when she performs tayammum and prays. This is based on istiḥsān (juristic preference).

f: 629. What was Muḥammad's opinion regarding the effect of tayammum on the husband's right of rajʿah?
b: Muḥammad held that the right of rajʿah ends as soon as she performs tayammum.

f: 630. Why did Muḥammad hold that tayammum ends the right of rajʿah?
b: He based this on qiyās, arguing that tayammum in the absence of water is a complete purification, and all rulings established through ghusl are also established through tayammum. Therefore, it replaces ghusl.

f: 631. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ not consider tayammum equivalent to ghusl for all rulings?
b: They argued that tayammum is not a true purification but a concession allowed due to necessity, and its effects only apply to the extent of that necessity.

f: 632. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ consider tayammum a concession rather than a complete purification?
b: Because tayammum only permits acts of worship that would otherwise be prevented, and the necessity exists during prayer, not before prayer begins.

f: 633. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, when exactly does the right of rajʿah end after tayammum?
b: There are two narrations: one says it ends immediately when she begins prayer, and another says it ends after she completes the prayer so that the permissibility of the prayer becomes established.

f: 634. If a woman performs ghusl after the third menstruation but forgets to wash part of her body, does the husband's right of rajʿah end?
b: It depends on the amount left unwashed: if it is a complete limb or more, the right of rajʿah does not end; if it is less than a limb, the right of rajʿah ends.

f: 635. What is the ruling if a woman leaves an entire limb or more unwashed during ghusl after her third menstruation?
b: Her husband's right of rajʿah remains because the missed washing is significant enough that her purity is not considered complete.

f: 636. What is the ruling if a woman leaves less than a limb unwashed during ghusl after her third menstruation?
b: Her husband's right of rajʿah ends because the small area is treated as having been washed for the purpose of ruling.

f: 637. Why does istiḥsān distinguish between leaving an entire limb and leaving less than a limb unwashed during ghusl?
b: Because a small area dries quickly due to its size, so it is uncertain whether water failed to reach it. A complete limb does not dry quickly and people normally do not overlook washing it.

f: 638. Why does qiyās suggest that leaving an entire limb unwashed should end the right of rajʿah?
b: Because most of the limb was washed, and qiyās would treat the remaining part as insignificant.

f: 639. Why does qiyās suggest that leaving less than a limb unwashed should preserve the right of rajʿah?
b: Because the rulings of janābah and menstruation are not divisible; either purification exists completely or it does not.

f: 640. Why does the Ḥanafī ruling regarding a small unwashed area take precaution in both matters?
b: They rule that rajʿah ends but she is not permitted to marry, ensuring caution regarding both the husband's right and the possibility of a new marriage.

f: 641. What was Abū Yūsuf's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ narration regarding leaving out rinsing the mouth and nose during ghusl?
b: One narration from Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ is that leaving out rinsing the mouth and nose is like leaving an entire limb unwashed.

f: 642. What was the other narration from Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding leaving out rinsing the mouth and nose during ghusl?
b: The other narration, which is also the view of Muḥammad, is that leaving them out is like leaving less than a limb because there is disagreement over whether they are obligatory, unlike the rest of the limbs.

f: 643. If a man divorces his pregnant wife or she gives birth to his child, and he claims, "I did not have intercourse with her," does he have the right of rajʿah?
b: Yes. He has the right of rajʿah because the pregnancy or child's lineage indicates that intercourse occurred.

f: 644. Why is pregnancy attributed to the husband if it occurs during a possible period?
b: Because of the statement of the Prophet ﷺ: "The child belongs to the marital bed," meaning that lineage is attributed to the husband.

f: 645. How does establishing the child's lineage prove that intercourse occurred?
b: Since the child is attributed to the husband, he is legally considered to have had intercourse, even if he denies it.

f: 646. Why does a husband's denial of intercourse not prevent rajʿah when pregnancy or the child's lineage exists?
b: Because the legal evidence of pregnancy or established lineage overrides his claim, as the child is attributed to the marital bed.

f: 647. Why does established intercourse strengthen the marital bond and establish the right of rajʿah?
b: Because intercourse strengthens the marital relationship, and a divorce occurring within a strengthened marital bond results in the right of rajʿah.

f: 648. Why is a husband's claim that he did not have intercourse rejected when pregnancy or lineage is established?
b: Because his claim contradicts the legal ruling established by the Sharīʿah, which considers the intercourse established through pregnancy or lineage.

f: 649. What additional legal ruling is established through confirmed intercourse besides rajʿah?
b: The ruling of iḥṣān (being legally considered chaste and protected from certain rulings) is established through confirmed intercourse.

f: 650. Why is the establishment of rajʿah through confirmed intercourse considered even more appropriate than the establishment of iḥṣān?
b: Because iḥṣān is a significant legal consequence of intercourse, so the continuation of the marital bond through rajʿah is even more deserving of recognition.

f: 651. If a woman gives birth in relation to a divorce case, when does the birth establish the possibility of rajʿah?
b: The intended case is when she gives birth before the divorce.

f: 652. Why does rajʿah not occur if the woman gives birth after the divorce?
b: Because giving birth after divorce completes the waiting period, and once the waiting period ends there is no longer any right of rajʿah.

f: 653. If a husband is alone with his wife, closes a door, lowers a curtain, denies intercourse, and then divorces her, does he have the right of rajʿah?
b: No. He does not have the right of rajʿah because he has admitted that intercourse, which strengthens the marital bond, did not occur.

f: 654. Why is the husband's statement accepted when he denies intercourse after seclusion (khalwah)?
b: Because rajʿah is his own right, and he is not contradicting any established legal ruling by denying intercourse.

f: 655. Why does denial of intercourse affect rajʿah but not the specified dowry?
b: Because the completion of the specified dowry is based on the delivery of the marital benefit through valid consummation/seclusion rules, not solely on actual physical intercourse.

f: 656. If a husband takes back his wife after seclusion and denying intercourse, and she gives birth less than two years minus one day later, is the rajʿah valid?
b: Yes. The rajʿah is valid because the child's lineage is established from him, meaning intercourse is legally considered to have occurred before the divorce.

f: 657. Why is lineage established when a child is born within less than two years minus one day after rajʿah?
b: Because the maximum possible pregnancy period allows the child to have remained in the womb for that length of time, so the child is attributed to the husband.

f: 658. Why is the intercourse assumed to have occurred before the divorce rather than after it in the case of a child born within two years?
b: Because if intercourse were assumed to have occurred after the divorce, the marital bond would have ended immediately and intercourse would have been prohibited, and a Muslim is not assumed to commit a prohibited act.

f: 659. If a husband says, "When you give birth, you are divorced," and she gives birth and later gives birth to another child, what is the ruling regarding rajʿah?
b: The second birth is considered a rajʿah, provided she has not admitted that her waiting period ended.

f: 660. How is it possible that the second child after the conditional divorce is from the husband?
b: The second child is from a new pregnancy that occurred during the waiting period after the first birth, meaning the husband had intercourse with her while rajʿah was still possible.

f: 661. What condition is required for the second birth after a conditional divorce to establish rajʿah?
b: The wife must not have admitted that her waiting period ended.

f: 662. Why does the second child after the first birth prove that the husband took her back?
b: Because the first birth caused the divorce and began the waiting period, and the second pregnancy occurred during that waiting period from intercourse with the husband.

f: 663. Can the second child after a conditional divorce occur more than two years after the first child and still establish rajʿah?
b: Yes. If she has not admitted the end of her waiting period, the second child may establish rajʿah even if it occurs after more than two years, because it is treated as a new pregnancy during the waiting period.

f: 664. If a man says, "Whenever you give birth to a child, you are divorced," and his wife gives birth to three children from different pregnancies, what happens with each birth?
b: The first child causes a divorce, the second child causes rajʿah, and the third child causes another divorce after which the waiting period is observed through menstrual cycles.

f: 665. Why does the first child cause a divorce in the case of the statement "Whenever you give birth to a child, you are divorced"?
b: Because the first birth fulfills the condition of the oath, causing the divorce to occur and making the woman one who is observing the waiting period.

f: 666. Why does the second child cause rajʿah in the case of repeated conditional divorce through childbirth?
b: Because the second pregnancy is attributed to intercourse during the waiting period, which means the husband is considered to have taken her back.

f: 667. Why does the second child also cause another divorce after rajʿah?
b: Because the word "whenever" (kullamā) makes the conditional divorce apply repeatedly each time the condition occurs.

f: 668. Why does the third child cause another rajʿah after the second divorce?
b: Because the third pregnancy is also attributed to intercourse during the waiting period after the second divorce, so the husband is considered to have taken her back again.

f: 669. Why does the third child result in a waiting period based on menstruation rather than pregnancy?
b: Because after the third child she is no longer pregnant and is a woman who menstruates, so her waiting period is counted through menstrual cycles.

f: 670. Does a woman divorced with a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) remain married to her husband during her waiting period?
b: Yes. The marriage remains established during the waiting period, which is why she is still lawful for her husband.

f: 671. Why is it recommended for a woman divorced with a revocable divorce to adorn herself and beautify herself?
b: Because she remains lawful for her husband, and beautification encourages him to take her back, which is recommended.

f: 672. Why is taking back a wife after a revocable divorce considered recommended?
b: Because preserving the marriage and returning to the marital relationship is encouraged when reconciliation is possible.

f: 673. Why is it recommended for a husband not to enter upon his wife after revocable divorce until he announces himself or makes her hear his footsteps?
b: So that he does not unexpectedly see her uncovered and unintentionally perform an action that would establish rajʿah.

f: 674. What problem may occur if a husband enters upon his wife without announcing himself after revocable divorce?
b: He may see something that causes rajʿah to occur unintentionally, then divorce her again, unnecessarily prolonging her waiting period.

f: 675. Does a husband have the right to travel with his revocably divorced wife before witnesses testify to his rajʿah?
b: According to the Ḥanafīs, he does not have this right until witnesses testify to his taking her back.

f: 676. What was Zufar's opinion regarding a husband travelling with his revocably divorced wife before witnesses testify to rajʿah?
b: Zufar held that he does have this right because the marriage bond remains established during the waiting period.

f: 677. Why do the Ḥanafīs allow intercourse with a revocably divorced wife even though they do not allow travelling with her before witnessed rajʿah?
b: Because the marriage remains established, and intercourse is considered an act specific to marriage that can itself establish rajʿah.

f: 678. What Qur'anic evidence do the Ḥanafīs use regarding the continued status of a revocably divorced woman?
b: They use the verse: "Do not expel them from their homes" (Qur'an 65:1), along with the remainder of the verse.

f: 679. Why does the delay of the divorce's full effect exist during the waiting period according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because the husband needs the opportunity to take her back during that period.

f: 680. What becomes clear if the husband does not take his wife back until the waiting period ends?
b: It becomes clear that he had no need for the possibility of taking her back, so the effect of the divorce is understood to have fully occurred from when it originally happened.

f: 681. Why are menstrual cycles counted as part of the waiting period even though the marriage bond remains during revocable divorce?
b: Because the delayed effect of the divorce continues during the waiting period until it becomes clear whether the husband will use his right of rajʿah.

f: 682. Why does the husband need witnesses to remove the wife's waiting period and establish full marital ownership again?
b: Because witnessed rajʿah cancels the waiting period and restores the husband's full marital authority.

f: 683. Is having witnesses for rajʿah obligatory according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No. According to the Ḥanafīs, witnessing rajʿah is recommended, not a condition for validity.

f: 684. What does the phrase "until he witnesses his taking her back" mean according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: It means that having witnesses present is recommended, based on the earlier discussion that rajʿah remains valid without witnesses.

f: 685. Does a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) make intercourse with the wife forbidden according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No. According to the Ḥanafīs, a revocable divorce does not make intercourse forbidden because the marriage bond remains established.

f: 686. What was Al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding intercourse after revocable divorce?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī held that intercourse becomes forbidden because the marriage ends due to the decisive effect of divorce.

f: 687. What is the Ḥanafī evidence that intercourse remains permissible after revocable divorce?
b: They argue that the marriage remains established because the husband possesses the right to take her back without her consent.

f: 688. Why does the husband's ability to take his wife back without her consent indicate that the marriage remains?
b: Because rajʿah was established for the husband's benefit, allowing him to correct the situation if he regrets the divorce, and this requires that he possesses independent authority over the marital bond.

f: 689. How do the Ḥanafīs explain the relationship between divorce and the continuation of marriage after ṭalāq rajʿī?
b: They explain that divorce has occurred, but its full nullifying effect is delayed until the waiting period ends. During that period, the marriage continues.

f: 690. Why is a revocable divorce considered a continuation of marriage rather than the creation of a new marriage?
b: Because the husband can restore the marriage through rajʿah without a new contract or the wife's consent.

f: 691. If a divorce is irrevocable (ṭalāq bāʾin) but fewer than three divorces, may the husband marry his divorced wife during her waiting period or after it ends?
b: Yes. He may marry her during the waiting period or after it ends because the quality of being a permissible marital partner remains.

f: 692. Why does an irrevocable divorce of fewer than three divorces not permanently prohibit the woman from her former husband?
b: Because permanent prohibition is connected to the third divorce, so it does not occur before the third divorce.

f: 693. Why is another man prohibited from marrying a woman during her waiting period after divorce, while the former husband may remarry her?
b: The prohibition of another man marrying her is due to possible confusion regarding lineage, but there is no such concern when the former husband remarries her.

f: 694. When does a divorced woman become permanently impermissible for her former husband according to the Qur'an?
b: She becomes impermissible after the third divorce (or the second divorce in the case of a slave woman) until she marries another husband through a valid marriage and that marriage ends.

f: 695. What is the evidence that a woman divorced three times cannot return to her first husband until she marries another man?
b: The evidence is the verse: "Then if he divorces her (for the third time), she is not lawful for him afterward until she marries another husband" (Qur'an 2:230).

f: 696. What is the intended meaning of "then if he divorces her" in the verse about a woman becoming impermissible?
b: The intended meaning is the third divorce, after which she becomes prohibited for her former husband until another valid marriage occurs.

f: 697. Why are two divorces for a slave woman equivalent to three divorces for a free woman?
b: Because slavery halves the amount of permissible marital ownership, so two divorces for a slave woman reach the same legal limit as three divorces for a free woman.

f: 698. What type of marriage to another man makes a woman permissible again for her first husband after three divorces?
b: It must be a valid, unrestricted marriage to another husband.

f: 699. Why is the phrase "until she marries another husband" understood as requiring a valid marriage contract?
b: Because the unrestricted state of being a wife is only established through a valid marriage contract.

f: 700. Does the woman become permissible for her first husband merely by marrying another man, or is intercourse also required?
b: Intercourse with the second husband is also required before she can return to her first husband.

f: 701. How is the requirement of intercourse derived from the Qur'anic verse about remarriage after three divorces?
b: The word "marriage" in the verse is interpreted as intercourse, because otherwise the verse would only repeat the requirement of a marriage contract, which is already understood from the word "husband."

f: 702. Why is the word "marriage" in the verse interpreted as intercourse rather than only a marriage contract?
b: Because interpreting it as intercourse gives an additional legal benefit and avoids redundancy in the wording of the verse.

f: 703. What additional evidence establishes that intercourse is required before a woman divorced three times can return to her first husband?
b: The evidence is the famous hadith: "She is not lawful for the first husband until she tastes the sweetness of the other husband," which has been transmitted through multiple chains.

f: 704. What does the hadith "until she tastes the sweetness of the other husband" mean according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: It means that the woman must have intercourse with the second husband before she becomes permissible again for the first husband.

f: 705. Did any scholar disagree with requiring intercourse with the second husband before returning to the first husband?
b: Yes. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib disagreed, but his opinion is not considered authoritative in this matter.

f: 706. What is the legal status of a judge's ruling if it is based on Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib's opinion that intercourse is not required?
b: Even if a judge ruled according to that opinion, the ruling would not be implemented because it contradicts the established position.

f: 707. Is penetration or ejaculation required for taḥlīl (making a woman permissible for her first husband) after three divorces?
b: Penetration is required; ejaculation is not a condition.

f: 708. Why is ejaculation not required for taḥlīl after three divorces?
b: Because ejaculation is a completion and an additional degree beyond the basic requirement of intercourse.

f: 709. What is the difference between penetration and ejaculation in the requirement of taḥlīl?
b: Penetration establishes the required intercourse, while ejaculation is an additional completion that is not necessary for the ruling.

f: 710. Is a young boy who is close to puberty considered capable of making a woman permissible for her first husband through intercourse?
b: Yes. According to the Ḥanafīs, a boy close to puberty is treated like an adult for taḥlīl if intercourse occurs in a valid marriage.

f: 711. What was Mālik's position regarding a boy close to puberty performing taḥlīl?
b: Mālik disagreed with the Ḥanafīs and did not consider such intercourse sufficient for taḥlīl.

f: 712. What is the Ḥanafī evidence that intercourse with a young boy close to puberty is sufficient for taḥlīl?
b: The condition established by the text is intercourse within a valid marriage, and that condition exists in this case.

f: 713. How is the case of a boy who has not reached puberty but is capable of intercourse explained in al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr?
b: If such a boy has intercourse with his wife, causing ghusl to become obligatory upon her, then she becomes permissible for her first husband.

f: 714. What is meant by a young boy being capable of intercourse in the context of taḥlīl?
b: It means that his sexual organ is active and he possesses sexual desire sufficient for intercourse.

f: 715. Why does ghusl become obligatory upon the woman after intercourse with a young boy?
b: Because the meeting of the circumcised parts occurs, which is the cause for the obligation of ghusl upon her.

f: 716. Why is ghusl not obligatory upon the young boy in this case, according to the discussion?
b: Because the legal requirement of ghusl does not apply to him in the same way, although he is instructed to perform it as a matter of good conduct.

f: 717. Does intercourse between a master and his slave woman make her permissible for her first husband after three divorces?
b: No. The intercourse of a master with his slave woman does not make her permissible for the first husband.

f: 718. Why does intercourse with a slave woman not count for taḥlīl after three divorces?
b: Because the Qur'anic condition is marriage to another husband, and the master-slave relationship is not marriage.

f: 719. What is the ruling if a man marries a woman on the condition that he will make her permissible for her first husband?
b: The marriage is disliked (makrūh).

f: 720. What evidence is given for the dislike of a marriage intended only for taḥlīl?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has cursed the one who makes her permissible and the one for whom she is made permissible."

f: 721. How do the Ḥanafīs interpret the hadith cursing the muḥallil and muḥallal lahu?
b: They interpret it as referring to a marriage whose purpose and condition is taḥlīl for the first husband, rather than a genuine marriage.

f: 722. If a man marries a woman after her three divorces and divorces her after having intercourse with her, does she become permissible for her first husband?
b: Yes. She becomes permissible for her first husband because intercourse occurred within a valid marriage.

f: 723. Why does a marriage intended for taḥlīl still make the woman permissible for her first husband according to the main Ḥanafī view?
b: Because the intercourse occurred within a valid marriage, and the marriage contract is not invalidated merely because of the condition attached to it.

f: 724. What was the narration from Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding a marriage contracted on the condition of taḥlīl?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ held that the marriage is invalid because it resembles a temporary marriage, and therefore it does not make the woman permissible for her first husband.

f: 725. Why did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ consider a conditional taḥlīl marriage invalid?
b: Because making the marriage conditional upon returning the woman to her first husband resembles a temporary arrangement rather than a genuine marriage.

f: 726. What was the narration from Muḥammad regarding a marriage contracted on the condition of taḥlīl?
b: Muḥammad held that the marriage is valid, but it does not make the woman permissible for her first husband.

f: 727. Why did Muḥammad say that a valid conditional taḥlīl marriage does not make the woman permissible for her first husband?
b: Because the husband hastened something that the Sharīʿah delayed, so he is punished by being prevented from achieving his intended objective.

f: 728. What analogy did Muḥammad use for preventing someone from achieving a result because of an improper action?
b: He compared it to a person who kills his inheritor and is prevented from inheriting because of his action.

f: 729. If a free woman is divorced once or twice, her waiting period ends, she marries another husband, and then returns to the first husband, how many divorces does she have available according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: She returns to the first husband with three divorces available. The second husband removes both fewer than three divorces and the full three divorces.

f: 730. What was Muḥammad's opinion regarding a woman who was divorced once or twice, married another man, and then returned to her first husband?
b: Muḥammad held that the second husband does not remove the previous divorces if they were fewer than three.

f: 731. What was Muḥammad's reasoning that a second husband does not remove divorces fewer than three?
b: He argued that the Qur'an sets three divorces as the limit for prohibition, so anything less than three is not included, and a prohibition cannot be removed before it exists.

f: 732. What is the evidence of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ that a second husband removes even fewer than three divorces?
b: Their evidence is the hadith cursing the one who makes a woman permissible and the one for whom she is made permissible, because it describes the second husband as the one who establishes permissibility.

f: 733. Why does calling the second husband "the one who makes her permissible" support the view of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Because it indicates that the second husband creates a new state of permissibility, removing the previous divorce restrictions.

f: 734. If a man divorces his wife three times and she claims that her waiting period ended, she married another man, he had intercourse with her, he divorced her, and her waiting period ended again, may the first husband believe her?
b: Yes. If the time period allows all of this to have occurred and he generally considers her truthful, he may believe her.

f: 735. Why may a husband accept his former wife's statement about her second marriage and divorce after three divorces?
b: Because it concerns a transaction or a religious ruling, since her permissibility depends upon it, and the statement of one person is accepted in such matters.

f: 736. Why is it not considered unlikely that the woman completed a second marriage, intercourse, divorce, and waiting period?
b: Because if the length of time allows these events to have occurred, there is no reason to reject her statement.

f: 737. What issue did the scholars differ about regarding a woman's claim that she became permissible after a second marriage?
b: They differed regarding the minimum amount of time required for the second marriage, intercourse, divorce, and waiting period to have occurred.

f: 738. Where is the discussion of the minimum time needed for a second marriage and waiting period found?
b: It is discussed in the chapter of waiting periods (ʿiddah).

f: 739. What is īlāʾ (the oath of abstention from the wife)?
b: Īlāʾ is when a husband swears an oath that he will not approach his wife.

f: 740. What statements make a man one who has made īlāʾ?
b: If he says, "By Allah, I will not approach you," or "By Allah, I will not approach you for four months," he has made īlāʾ.

f: 741. What is the evidence for the ruling of īlāʾ?
b: The evidence is the verse: "For those who swear oaths of abstention from their wives is a waiting period of four months" (Qur'an 2:226).

f: 742. What happens if a man who made īlāʾ has intercourse with his wife within the four months?
b: He breaks his oath, expiation becomes obligatory upon him, and the īlāʾ ends.

f: 743. Why does expiation become obligatory when a man breaks his oath of īlāʾ?
b: Because expiation is the legal consequence of breaking an oath.

f: 744. Why does īlāʾ end when the husband has intercourse with his wife?
b: Because the oath has been broken and its purpose of preventing intercourse no longer exists.

f: 745. What happens if a husband does not approach his wife until four months pass after making īlāʾ?
b: According to the Ḥanafīs, she becomes separated from him through one divorce.

f: 746. What was Al-Shāfiʿī's opinion regarding separation after four months of īlāʾ?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī held that separation occurs through the decree of a judge because the husband is preventing her right of intercourse.

f: 747. Why did Al-Shāfiʿī compare īlāʾ to castration or impotence?
b: Because in all these cases the husband prevents the wife's right to intercourse, so the judge acts on her behalf to release her.

f: 748. What is the Ḥanafī evidence that divorce occurs automatically after four months of īlāʾ?
b: They argue that the husband wronged his wife by preventing her right, so the Sharīʿah removes the blessing of marriage from him when the period ends.

f: 749. Which Companions' practice supports the Ḥanafī ruling regarding īlāʾ?
b: It was transmitted from ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, the three ʿAbdullāhs, and Zayd ibn Thābit that separation occurs after the four-month period.

f: 750. Why do the Ḥanafīs consider the practice of these Companions sufficient evidence?
b: Because they are examples to be followed in legal rulings and their transmitted practice supports the ruling.

f: 751. How was īlāʾ treated during the time of ignorance?
b: Īlāʾ was a form of divorce during the time of ignorance.
