b: No. One act cannot fulfil two separate obligations at the same time, so he may assign it to whichever obligation he wishes.

f: 1151. If a person fasts two months for two ẓihār kaffārahs, can it fulfil both simultaneously?
b: No. He may assign the fasting to whichever obligation he wishes.

f: 1152. If a person frees one slave intending both a ẓihār kaffārah and a killing kaffārah, does it count for either?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and the two companions, no. It does not count for either because the two kaffārahs are different categories and he did not specify one.

f: 1153. What is Zufar's view regarding performing one kaffārah act for two obligations?
b: He says it is not sufficient in either case, because the person has already divided the act between the obligations and cannot later assign it.

f: 1154. What is al-Shāfiʿī's view regarding performing one kaffārah act for two obligations?
b: He says he may assign it to whichever obligation he wishes in both cases, because all kaffārahs share the same objective.

f: 1155. Why does the Ḥanafī school distinguish between two obligations of the same type and two different types of kaffārah?
b: Because intention of specification has no effect within the same category, but it has effect when the categories differ.

f: 1156. What is an example where specification of intention is unnecessary due to the obligations being the same type?
b: If someone fasts one day intending to make up two missed Ramaḍān fasts, it counts as making up one day.

f: 1157. What is an example where specification of intention is necessary due to different types of obligations?
b: If someone owes both a missed obligatory fast and a vowed fast, he must distinguish between them through intention.

f: 1158. What is the ruling if a man accuses his wife of adultery, both spouses are qualified for testimony, she is someone whose accuser would receive the punishment for false accusation, or he denies the lineage of her child, and she demands the consequence of the accusation?
b: Liʿān becomes required upon him.

f: 1159. What is liʿān according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Liʿān consists of confirmed testimonies strengthened by oaths and accompanied by a curse. It replaces the punishment of false accusation for the husband and the punishment of adultery for the wife.

f: 1160. What Qur’anic verse establishes the basis of liʿān?
b: Allah says: "And those who accuse their wives but have no witnesses except themselves..." (Qur'an 24:6).

f: 1161. What are the essential elements of liʿān according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: The essential pillar is testimony strengthened by oath. The husband's testimony is accompanied by the curse if he is lying, and the wife's testimony is accompanied by anger if he is lying.

f: 1162. Why is the husband's curse included in liʿān?
b: Because it takes the place of the punishment for false accusation that would otherwise apply to him.

f: 1163. Why is the wife's anger included in liʿān?
b: Because it takes the place of the punishment for adultery that would otherwise apply to her.

f: 1164. Why must both spouses be qualified for testimony for liʿān to apply?
b: Because the foundation of liʿān is testimony, so both parties must possess the qualification of testimony.

f: 1165. Why must the wife be someone whose accuser would receive the punishment for false accusation?
b: Because liʿān replaces the punishment for false accusation against the husband, and this requires that she be legally protected (muḥṣanah).

f: 1166. When does denying the child's lineage also require liʿān?
b: When the husband denies that the child belongs to him, because this outwardly implies an accusation of adultery against the wife.

f: 1167. Why is denying the child's lineage considered an accusation of adultery?
b: Because lineage is originally established through the marital bed, and denying a child from a valid marriage bed implies that the child came through unlawful intercourse.

f: 1168. Is the possibility that the child came from intercourse due to a mistaken belief of permissibility considered in denying lineage?
b: No. This possibility is not considered.

f: 1169. Why is denying lineage from a valid marriage bed treated as an accusation?
b: Because the foundation of lineage is the valid marriage bed, and even a defective marriage bed is attached to it unless the child is proven to belong elsewhere.

f: 1170. If a person has two obligations of ẓihār expiation and frees two slaves without specifying which one is for which obligation, is it valid?
b: It is valid for both obligations. Likewise, if he fasts four months or feeds one hundred and twenty poor people, it is valid. This is because the type is the same, so a specific intention is unnecessary.

f: 1171. If he frees one slave for both obligations, or fasts two months, what happens?
b: He may assign it to whichever one he wishes, because one act cannot fulfil two obligations simultaneously.

f: 1172. If he frees a slave intending both ẓihār expiation and a killing expiation, does it count?
b: It does not count for either one. This is because these are two different types of expiation, and the intention was not specified for one of them.

f: 1173. What did Zufar say regarding intending both ẓihār and killing expiation?
b: He said that it is not sufficient for either obligation in both cases.

f: 1174. What did al-Shāfiʿī say regarding intending both types of expiation?
b: He said that he may assign it to whichever one he wishes in both cases, because all expiations, considering their objective, are one category.

f: 1175. What is the reasoning of Zufar?
b: He said that he freed half of the slave on behalf of each obligation. He does not have the right to assign it to one after already freeing it for both because the matter has left his control.

f: 1176. What is our evidence regarding intention in expiations?
b: The intention of specification within the same category has no benefit, so it is disregarded. However, within different categories it has benefit.

f: 1177. Give an example where specification within the same category is unnecessary.
b: If a person fasts one day intending to make up two missed Ramaḍān fasts, it suffices for the make-up of one day.

f: 1178. Give an example where distinction between categories is necessary.
b: If a person owes both a missed obligatory fast and a vowed fast, distinction between them is necessary.

f: 1179. What is the foundation of liʿān according to us?
b: Liʿān consists of confirmed testimonies strengthened by oaths and accompanied by the curse. It takes the place of the punishment for false accusation regarding him and the punishment for adultery regarding her.

f: 1180. What verse establishes liʿān?
b: Allah says: "And those who accuse their wives but have no witnesses except themselves..." (Qur'an 24:6).

f: 1181. What is the essential pillar of liʿān?
b: The essential pillar is testimony strengthened by oath.

f: 1182. Why must both husband and wife be qualified for testimony in liʿān?
b: Because the essential element of liʿān is testimony.

f: 1183. Why must the wife be someone whose accuser would receive the punishment for false accusation?
b: Because liʿān replaces the punishment for false accusation against him, so her being protected (muḥṣanah) is necessary.

f: 1184. Does denial of the child's lineage also require liʿān?
b: Yes. This is because denying her child outwardly amounts to accusing her of adultery.

f: 1185. Why is the wife's request a condition for liʿān?
b: Because it is her right, and rights require the request of the one entitled to them.

f: 1186. If the husband refuses to perform liʿān, what does the judge do?
b: The judge imprisons him until he either performs liʿān or admits that he lied.

f: 1187. If the husband performs liʿān, what becomes required upon the wife?
b: Liʿān becomes obligatory upon her.

f: 1188. If the wife refuses liʿān, what does the judge do?
b: The judge imprisons her until she performs liʿān or confirms his accusation.

f: 1189. If the husband is a slave, disbeliever, or someone previously punished for false accusation and he accuses his wife, what happens?
b: He receives the punishment for false accusation because liʿān is impossible due to a deficiency on his side.

f: 1190. What is the method of liʿān?
b: The judge begins with the husband. He testifies four times, saying each time: "I testify by Allah that I am among those who are truthful regarding what I accused her of concerning adultery."

f: 1191. What does the husband say in the fifth testimony?
b: "The curse of Allah is upon him if he is among the liars regarding what he accused her of concerning adultery."

f: 1192. What does the husband do while performing liʿān?
b: He points towards her during all of this.

f: 1193. What does the wife say during the first four testimonies of liʿān?
b: She says each time: "I testify by Allah that he is among those who are liars regarding what he accused me of concerning adultery."

f: 1194. What does the wife say in the fifth testimony?
b: She says: "The anger of Allah is upon her if he is among those who are truthful regarding what he accused me of concerning adultery."

f: 1195. What is the basis for the wording of the wife's liʿān?
b: The basis is the text previously mentioned regarding liʿān.

f: 1196. What wording does al-Ḥasan narrate from Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding liʿān?
b: He narrates that Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ uses the direct address wording: "Regarding what I accused you of concerning adultery."

f: 1197. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ use the direct address wording?
b: Because it removes possibility and ambiguity more clearly.

f: 1198. How is ambiguity removed when using third-person wording in liʿān?
b: The third-person wording, when accompanied by pointing, removes ambiguity.

f: 1199. When husband and wife perform liʿān, does separation occur immediately?
b: No. Separation does not occur until the judge separates them.

f: 1200. What did Zufar say regarding separation after liʿān?
b: He said that separation occurs through their mutual liʿān because permanent prohibition is established through the hadith.

f: 1201. What is our evidence that the judge must separate them?
b: The establishment of prohibition prevents maintaining the marriage properly. Therefore, he must release her with kindness. If he refuses, the judge takes his place to remove injustice.

f: 1202. What statement from the man who performed liʿān before the Prophet ﷺ supports this?
b: He said: "I would be lying about her, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If I keep her, then she is divorced three times." He said this after the liʿān.

f: 1203. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad, what type of separation occurs after liʿān?
b: It is one irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bāʾin).

f: 1204. Why is the separation considered one irrevocable divorce according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: Because the action of the judge is attributed to the husband, just as in the case of impotence (ʿunnah).

f: 1205. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad, can the husband marry her again if he admits that he lied?
b: Yes, he may propose to her again if he admits he lied.

f: 1206. What did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say regarding reunion after liʿān?
b: He said that the prohibition is permanent and they cannot reunite.

f: 1207. What is Abū Yūsuf's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ evidence?
b: The statement of the Prophet ﷺ: "The two who perform liʿān will never reunite." He understood this as explicitly indicating permanence.

f: 1208. What is the evidence of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: Admitting he lied is a retraction, and a testimony after retraction has no legal effect.

f: 1209. Why can they reunite after the husband admits he lied according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: Because after his admission, the liʿān and its ruling no longer remain. Therefore, they can reunite.

f: 1210. If the accusation was by denying the child, what does the judge do?
b: The judge denies his lineage and attaches the child to the mother.

f: 1211. What is the form of liʿān when the accusation is by denying the child?
b: The judge orders the man, and he says: "I testify by Allah that I am among those who are truthful regarding what I accused you of concerning denial of the child." The woman does the same.

f: 1212. If the husband accused her of adultery and also denied the child, what does he mention in liʿān?
b: He mentions both matters in the liʿān. Then the judge denies the child's lineage and attaches it to the mother.

f: 1213. What narration supports the judge denying the child's lineage in this case?
b: The narration that the Prophet ﷺ denied the child of the wife of Hilāl ibn Umayyah from Hilāl and attached it to her.

f: 1214. What is the purpose of liʿān when it concerns denial of the child?
b: The purpose is denying the child, so his objective is fulfilled through the judge's ruling of separation.

f: 1215. According to Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, what does the judge say when denying the child's lineage?
b: He separates them and says: "The mother has claimed him and removed him from the father's lineage."

f: 1216. Why does Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say the judge must mention that the mother removed him from the father's lineage?
b: Because the child becomes detached from him, so this must be mentioned.

f: 1217. If the husband later admits he lied, what does the judge do?
b: The judge punishes him because he has admitted that the punishment is due upon him.

f: 1218. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad, may the husband marry her after admitting he lied?
b: Yes, it is permissible for him to marry her.

f: 1219. Why may they reunite after his admission of lying according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: Because once he is punished, he is no longer qualified for liʿān, so its ruling — permanent prohibition — is removed.

f: 1220. What other cases are compared to the husband admitting he lied?
b: If he accuses another woman and is punished, or if she commits adultery and is punished, because their eligibility for liʿān is removed.

f: 1221. If the husband accuses his wife while she is a child or insane, is liʿān performed?
b: No, there is no liʿān between them.

f: 1222. Why is there no liʿān if the wife is a child or insane?
b: Because if a stranger accused her, he would not receive the punishment for false accusation. Therefore, the husband does not perform liʿān either, since it replaces that punishment.

f: 1223. If the husband himself is a child or insane, is liʿān performed?
b: No, because he lacks eligibility for testimony.

f: 1224. Why does the accusation of a mute person not involve liʿān?
b: Because liʿān is connected to explicit speech, like the punishment for false accusation.

f: 1225. What is al-Shāfiʿī's position regarding a mute person's accusation?
b: He disagrees.

f: 1226. What is our reasoning regarding doubtful accusations in liʿān?
b: It contains doubt, and punishments are removed through doubt.

f: 1227. If the husband says: "This pregnancy is not from me," is liʿān required?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Zufar, no liʿān is required.

f: 1228. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say there is no liʿān when he denies the pregnancy?
b: Because the existence of pregnancy is not certain, so he has not become an accuser.

f: 1229. What do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad say regarding denial of pregnancy?
b: They say liʿān is required if she gives birth less than six months later.

f: 1230. Why do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad require liʿān if she gives birth within less than six months?
b: Because then the existence of the pregnancy is certain and the accusation is established.

f: 1231. What is the response according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Zufar?
b: If it is not an accusation at the present time, it is like attaching it to a condition: "If you are pregnant, then it is not from me." An accusation cannot be conditional.

f: 1232. If he says: "You committed adultery and this pregnancy is from adultery," what happens?
b: They perform liʿān because he has explicitly mentioned adultery, establishing the accusation.

f: 1233. Does the judge deny the pregnancy?
b: No, the judge does not deny the pregnancy.

f: 1234. What does al-Shāfiʿī say regarding denying the pregnancy before birth?
b: He says the judge denies it because the Prophet ﷺ denied Hilāl's child while he had accused her while pregnant.

f: 1235. What is the Hanafi evidence that legal rulings are not attached before birth?
b: Legal rulings are not attached until after birth because uncertainty remains before then.

f: 1236. How do the Hanafis interpret the narration of Hilāl's child?
b: The narration is interpreted as meaning that the pregnancy was known through revelation.

f: 1237. When is the husband's denial of his wife's child valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: If he denies it immediately after birth, during the time when congratulations are normally accepted, or when childbirth items are purchased, his denial is valid and liʿān occurs.

f: 1238. What happens if he denies the child after that according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Liʿān occurs but lineage is established.

f: 1239. What do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad say regarding the period of denial?
b: His denial is valid throughout the period of postnatal bleeding.

f: 1240. Why do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad use the period of postnatal bleeding?
b: Because denial is valid in a short period but not a long one, so they distinguished it by the period connected to childbirth.

f: 1241. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ not specify a fixed time period?
b: Because people differ in their circumstances and reflection, so there is no fixed meaning to a specific time limit.

f: 1242. What signs indicate acceptance of the child according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Accepting congratulations, remaining silent when congratulated, buying childbirth necessities, or allowing that time to pass.

f: 1243. If the husband was absent and did not know of the birth, when is the period considered?
b: After returning, the previously mentioned period is considered according to both views.

f: 1244. If she gives birth to two children from one pregnancy and he denies the first but acknowledges the second, what is the ruling?
b: Both lineages are established.

f: 1245. Why are both lineages established in the case of twins?
b: Because they are twins, created from one fluid.

f: 1246. Why is the husband punished when he denies the first twin but acknowledges the second?
b: Because by acknowledging the second, he has contradicted himself.

f: 1247. If he acknowledges the first child and denies the second, what happens?
b: Both lineages are established, and he performs liʿān.

f: 1248. Why does liʿān apply when he denies the second child?
b: Because he is accusing her by denying the second child and has not retracted that accusation.

f: 1249. Why does his earlier acknowledgement of the first child not prevent liʿān?
b: Because his earlier acknowledgement of her chastity occurred before the accusation. This is like saying: "She is chaste," then saying: "She is an adulterer."

f: 1250. What is the ruling if a husband is impotent and unable to have intercourse with his wife?
b: The judge gives him one year. If he reaches her during that year, this is accepted. Otherwise, they are separated if she requests it.

f: 1251. Who narrated the ruling that an impotent husband is given one year?
b: It is narrated from ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, ʿAlī, and Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them.

f: 1252. Why is an impotent husband given one year before separation?
b: Because the wife has a right to intercourse, and the inability may be due to a temporary condition or an inherent defect. A period is needed to determine whether the inability is permanent.

f: 1253. Why was the period of one year chosen for an impotent husband?
b: Because one year contains all four seasons.

f: 1254. What does the passing of one year without intercourse prove regarding the impotent husband?
b: It proves that his inability is due to a permanent defect.

f: 1255. What is the legal consequence if an impotent husband remains unable to have intercourse after one year?
b: Maintaining the marriage properly is no longer possible, so he must release her with kindness. If he refuses, the judge separates them.

f: 1256. Why is the wife's request required before separation due to her husband's impotence?
b: Because separation is her right.

f: 1257. What type of divorce results when the judge separates an impotent husband from his wife?
b: It is an irrevocable divorce.

f: 1258. Why is separation due to impotence considered an irrevocable divorce according to the Hanafis?
b: Because the judge's action is attributed to the husband, as though he divorced her himself.

f: 1259. Why do the Hanafis disagree with al-Shāfiʿī regarding separation due to impotence?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī considers it annulment, while the Hanafis hold that marriage cannot be annulled in this case.

f: 1260. Why is the divorce due to impotence irrevocable according to the Hanafis?
b: Because the purpose of removing harm from the wife would not be achieved if the husband could simply take her back.

f: 1261. Does seclusion between an impotent husband and his wife count as valid seclusion?
b: Yes, the seclusion of an impotent husband is valid.

f: 1262. What dowry does a wife receive if her impotent husband had valid seclusion with her?
b: She receives her full dowry.

f: 1263. Is the waiting period obligatory for a woman separated from an impotent husband?
b: Yes, the waiting period is obligatory.

f: 1264. When does the ruling of full dowry and waiting period apply in the case of impotence?
b: It applies when the husband admits that he did not have intercourse with her.

f: 1265. If a husband and wife disagree about whether intercourse occurred and the wife was previously married, whose statement is accepted?
b: The husband's statement is accepted along with an oath.

f: 1266. Why is the husband's statement accepted when a previously married wife claims intercourse occurred?
b: Because he denies that she has a right to separation, and the original assumption is that he is physically capable.

f: 1267. What happens if a husband swears that intercourse did not occur with his previously married wife?
b: The wife's right to separation is cancelled.

f: 1268. What happens if a husband refuses to swear when his previously married wife claims intercourse occurred?
b: He is given one year.

f: 1269. How is the occurrence of intercourse investigated if the wife is a virgin and the husband claims intercourse occurred?
b: Women examine her condition.

f: 1270. What happens if women examining a virgin wife say that she is still a virgin?
b: The husband is given one year.

f: 1271. Why is an impotent husband given one year if the wife is still found to be a virgin?
b: Because his claim that intercourse occurred appears false.

f: 1272. What happens if women examining a virgin wife say that she is no longer a virgin?
b: The husband is asked to swear.

f: 1273. What happens if the husband swears after women testify that the wife is no longer a virgin?
b: The wife has no right to separation.

f: 1274. What happens if the husband refuses to swear after women testify that the wife is no longer a virgin?
b: He is given one year.

f: 1275. If the husband is castrated, when are the spouses separated?
b: They are separated immediately if she requests it, because there is no benefit in waiting.

f: 1276. Why is the eunuch given a delay like the impotent man?
b: Because intercourse from him is still possible.

f: 1277. If the husband swears that he will not give his wife the option, and she was originally a non-virgin, whose statement is accepted?
b: The statement of the husband is accepted along with his oath.

f: 1278. If the wife chooses to remain with her husband during the waiting period, can she exercise her option later?
b: No. She no longer has any option afterwards because she accepted the loss of her right.

f: 1279. What type of year is considered for the waiting period in the case of the husband's option?
b: The lunar year is considered according to the correct view.

f: 1280. Are menstruation days and Ramadan counted within the waiting period?
b: Yes. They are counted because they are part of the year.

f: 1281. Are the illnesses of the husband or wife counted within the waiting period?
b: No. They are not counted because a year may pass without such illnesses occurring.

f: 1282. Does a husband have the option to annul the marriage due to defects in his wife?
b: No. The husband has no option of annulment due to defects in his wife.

f: 1283. Which defects did Imam al-Shafi'i say allow annulment?
b: He said five defects allow this: leprosy, vitiligo, insanity, vaginal obstruction (ratq), and vaginal closure/abnormality (qarn).

f: 1284. Why did Imam al-Shafi'i allow annulment due to these defects?
b: Because they prevent the husband from fulfilling his marital rights physically or naturally, and natural aversion is supported by the Sacred Law.

f: 1285. What evidence did Imam al-Shafi'i use regarding leprosy?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Flee from the leper as you flee from a lion."

f: 1286. What is the Hanafi response to the argument that defects require annulment?
b: The complete loss of marital enjoyment due to death does not require annulment, so lesser deficiencies do not deserve annulment either.

f: 1287. Why does the Hanafi school not consider these defects sufficient for annulment?
b: Because consummation is one of the benefits of marriage, but the actual right owed is the ability to have access, and that remains present.

f: 1288. Does a wife have the option if her husband has insanity, vitiligo, or leprosy according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: No. According to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, she does not have the option.

f: 1289. What is Muhammad's view regarding a wife whose husband has insanity, vitiligo, or leprosy?
b: Muhammad said that she does have the option.

f: 1290. What is Muhammad's reasoning for allowing annulment due to these defects?
b: It is to prevent harm from reaching her, similar to the cases of castration and impotence.

f: 1291. Why did Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ not establish an option for these defects?
b: The basic principle is that there is no option of annulment because it nullifies the husband's right. It is only established where the main purpose of marriage is prevented, such as castration and impotence.

f: 1292. What is the waiting period (ʿiddah) of a free woman who menstruates after divorce or separation?
b: Her waiting period is three menstrual cycles.

f: 1293. What is the evidence for the waiting period of three menstrual cycles?
b: The statement of Allah: "Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quruʾ." (Qur'an 2:228)

f: 1294. Why is separation without divorce treated like divorce regarding ʿiddah?
b: Because the purpose of ʿiddah is to establish whether the womb is free of pregnancy after separation from marriage, and this applies in both cases.

f: 1295. What does the Hanafi school understand by the word quruʾ?
b: The Hanafi school understands quruʾ to mean menstruations.

f: 1296. What does Imam al-Shafi'i understand by quruʾ?
b: Imam al-Shafi'i understands quruʾ to mean periods of purity (ṭuhr).

f: 1297. Why did Imam al-Shafi'i interpret quruʾ as purity?
b: Because the word is a homonym that can refer to both menstruation and purity, and he considered purity the intended meaning.

f: 1298. Why do the Hanafis prefer the meaning of menstruation for quruʾ?
b: Because the plural form fits better, menstruation indicates the clearing of the womb, and the Prophet ﷺ clarified that the waiting period of a slave woman is two menstruations.

f: 1299. What is the waiting period of a woman who does not menstruate due to young age or old age?
b: Her waiting period is three months.

f: 1300. What is the evidence for the waiting period of three months for women who do not menstruate?
b: The statement of Allah: "And those women who have despaired of menstruation among your women — if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months…" (Qur'an 65:4)

f: 1301. Does the three-month waiting period include a woman who has reached menstruating age but never menstruated?
b: Yes. It includes a woman who reaches the normal age of menstruation but has never menstruated.

f: 1302. What is the waiting period of a pregnant woman after divorce or separation?
b: Her waiting period ends when she gives birth.

f: 1303. What is the evidence that the waiting period of a pregnant woman ends with childbirth?
b: Allah’s statement: “And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.” (Qur’an 65:4)

f: 1304. What is the waiting period of a slave woman after divorce?
b: Her waiting period is two menstruations.

f: 1305. What is the evidence for the waiting period of two menstruations for a slave woman?
b: The statement of the Prophet ﷺ: “The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces, and her waiting period is two menstruations.”

f: 1306. Why is the waiting period of a slave woman two menstruations instead of one menstruation?
b: Because slavery halves certain legal rulings, but a menstruation cannot be divided, so it is completed as two menstruations.

f: 1307. What did ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ say regarding halving the menstruation period of a slave woman?
b: He said: “If I were able, I would have made it one menstruation and half.”

f: 1308. What is the waiting period of a slave woman who does not menstruate?
b: Her waiting period is one and a half months.

f: 1309. Why is the waiting period of a non-menstruating slave woman one and a half months?
b: Because months can be divided, so half of the free woman's waiting period is applied due to slavery.

f: 1310. What is the waiting period of a free woman whose husband dies?
b: Four months and ten days.

f: 1311. What is the evidence for the waiting period of a widow?
b: Allah’s statement: “Those among you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days.” (Qur’an 2:234)

f: 1312. What is the waiting period of a slave woman whose husband dies?
b: Two months and five days, because slavery halves the period.

f: 1313. What is the waiting period of a pregnant woman whose husband dies?
b: Her waiting period is until she gives birth.

f: 1314. What evidence supports that a pregnant widow’s waiting period ends with childbirth?
b: The general wording of Allah: “And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.” (Qur’an 65:4)

f: 1315. What did ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ say regarding the revelation order of Sūrat al-Ṭalāq and the waiting period verse?
b: He said: “Whoever wishes, I will challenge him to a mutual invocation that the shorter chapter of women (Sūrat al-Ṭalāq) was revealed after the verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah.”

f: 1316. What did ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ say about a pregnant woman whose husband dies?
b: He said: “Even if she gave birth while her husband was lying on his funeral bed, her waiting period would end and she would become permitted to marry.”

f: 1317. What is the waiting period of a woman divorced during her husband’s terminal illness if she inherits from him according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad?
b: Her waiting period is the longer of the two periods: the waiting period of divorce or the waiting period of widowhood.

f: 1318. What is Abu Yusuf’s رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ view regarding the waiting period of a woman divorced during her husband’s terminal illness who inherits from him?
b: Her waiting period is three menstruations if the divorce was irrevocable or three divorces.

f: 1319. According to Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, what is the waiting period if the divorce during terminal illness was revocable?
b: She observes the waiting period of widowhood by consensus according to Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.

f: 1320. Why does Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say a woman with a revocable divorce observes the waiting period of widowhood after her husband dies?
b: Because the marriage ended through death, while the three menstruation waiting period only applies when separation occurs through divorce.

f: 1321. Why do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad say the woman divorced during terminal illness observes the longer of the two waiting periods?
b: Because the marriage remains for inheritance purposes, so it is treated as remaining for the waiting period as a precaution, combining both rulings.

f: 1322. If a husband is killed due to apostasy and his wife inherits from him, what waiting period does she follow?
b: The same disagreement applies between Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad on one side and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ on the other.

f: 1323. What other view exists regarding the waiting period of the wife of someone killed due to apostasy?
b: It has been said that her waiting period is by menstruation according to consensus.

f: 1324. Why was it said that the wife of someone killed due to apostasy follows the menstruation waiting period by consensus?
b: Because the marriage was considered remaining until death for inheritance purposes, since a Muslim woman does not inherit from a disbeliever.

f: 1325. If a slave woman is freed during her waiting period after a revocable divorce, does her waiting period change?
b: Yes. Her waiting period changes to that of free women.

f: 1326. Why does a freed slave woman after revocable divorce receive the waiting period of free women?
b: Because the marriage remains intact in every respect.

f: 1327. If a slave woman is freed while observing the waiting period after irrevocable divorce, does her waiting period change?
b: No. Her waiting period does not change.

f: 1328. If a slave woman is freed while observing the waiting period after her husband’s death, does her waiting period change?
b: No. Her waiting period does not change.

f: 1329. Why does freedom not change the waiting period after irrevocable divorce or death?
b: Because the marriage has already ended through irrevocable separation or death.

f: 1330. If an elderly woman who has despaired of menstruation completes her waiting period by months and then sees blood, what happens to her waiting period?
b: The previous waiting period is invalidated, and she must restart her waiting period through menstruation.

f: 1331. When does the return of menstruation invalidate the waiting period calculated by months?
b: When she sees blood according to her normal cycle, because this removes the assumption of menopause.

f: 1332. Why is the previous calculation by months not considered a true substitute after menstruation returns?
b: Because relying on menopause requires certainty of permanent inability to menstruate, which is only established by its continuation until death.

f: 1333. What analogy is mentioned regarding the uncertainty of menopause?
b: It is compared to the ruling of an elderly person who cannot fast, where the inability is only certain through continuation.

f: 1334. If a woman menstruated twice and then reached menopause, how does she complete her waiting period?
b: She observes the waiting period by months.

f: 1335. Why does a woman who menstruated twice and then reached menopause complete her waiting period by months?
b: To avoid combining the substitute (badal) with the original obligation (mubdal).

f: 1336. What is the waiting period of a woman married through an invalid marriage (nikāḥ fāsid)?
b: Her waiting period is calculated by menstruations.

f: 1337. What is the waiting period of a woman who had intercourse due to a mistaken assumption (waṭʾ bi-shubha)?
b: Her waiting period is calculated by menstruations.

f: 1338. Does the waiting period for an invalid marriage or intercourse due to mistaken assumption differ between separation and death?
b: No. In both cases it is through menstruation.

f: 1339. Why is the waiting period for an invalid marriage and waṭʾ bi-shubha based on menstruation?
b: Because the purpose of the waiting period is to establish that the womb is free of pregnancy, and menstruation indicates this.

f: 1340. What is the waiting period of an umm walad if her master dies or frees her?
b: Three menstruations.

f: 1341. What was Imam al-Shafi'i's view regarding the waiting period of an umm walad?
b: He said it is one menstruation because it is due to the removal of ownership (milk al-yamīn).

f: 1342. Why did Imam al-Shafi'i compare the waiting period of an umm walad to istibrāʾ?
b: Because both are connected to establishing purity of the womb after ownership ends.

f: 1343. What is the Hanafi evidence that an umm walad's waiting period is three menstruations?
b: It is because the waiting period is connected to the ending of the marital bond (firāsh), so it resembles the waiting period of marriage.

f: 1344. Which Companion did the Hanafi Imam follow regarding the waiting period of an umm walad?
b: ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, who said: “The waiting period of an umm walad is three menstruations.”

f: 1345. If an umm walad is among those who do not menstruate, what is her waiting period?
b: Three months, just as in a valid marriage.

f: 1346. If a minor husband dies leaving behind a pregnant wife, what is her waiting period according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad?
b: Her waiting period is until she gives birth.

f: 1347. What is Abu Yusuf's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ view regarding a pregnant wife of a deceased minor husband?
b: Her waiting period is four months and ten days.

f: 1348. What is Imam al-Shafi'i's view regarding the waiting period of a pregnant wife of a deceased minor husband?
b: His view is also that her waiting period is four months and ten days.

f: 1349. What is the argument of Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Imam al-Shafi'i regarding the pregnancy of a wife of a minor husband?
b: The pregnancy is not established as his lineage, so it is like a pregnancy occurring after his death.

f: 1350. What is the Hanafi evidence that the waiting period of the pregnant wife of a minor husband ends with childbirth?
b: The unrestricted statement of Allah: “And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.” (Qur’an 65:4)

f: 1351. Why do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad say the waiting period of a pregnant woman is always connected to childbirth?
b: Because the Law connected the waiting period of pregnant women to childbirth, whether the pregnancy period is short or long.

f: 1352. Why do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad say the waiting period is not merely for determining whether the womb is empty?
b: Because the Law established waiting periods by months even for women who menstruate, showing that another purpose exists.

f: 1353. What additional purpose do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad mention for the waiting period?
b: Fulfilling the right connected to marriage, and this exists even in the case of a minor husband.

f: 1354. Why does the Hanafi school distinguish a pregnancy after death from the case of a pregnant wife of a minor husband?
b: Because in a normal marriage lineage can be established from the husband, so the pregnancy is legally treated as existing at death, unlike the case of a minor husband.

f: 1355. Is the lineage of the child established from a minor husband in this case?
b: No. The child’s lineage is not established because a child has no reproductive fluid, so conception from him is impossible.

f: 1356. Why can marriage establish lineage despite the absence of reproductive ability in some cases?
b: Because marriage takes the place of biological possibility where conception is legally possible.

f: 1357. If a man divorces his wife while she is menstruating, does the menstruation in which the divorce occurred count as part of her waiting period?
b: No. She does not count that menstruation as part of her waiting period.

f: 1358. Why does the menstruation during which divorce occurred not count toward the waiting period?
b: Because the waiting period is defined as three complete menstruations, and it cannot be reduced.

f: 1359. If a woman in waiting period has intercourse due to a mistaken assumption (waṭʾ bi-shubha), must she observe another waiting period?
b: Yes. She must observe another waiting period.

f: 1360. Do the first and second waiting periods overlap after intercourse due to a mistaken assumption?
b: Yes. According to the Hanafi school, they overlap.

f: 1361. How do the menstruations experienced during two overlapping waiting periods count?
b: Any menstruation she experiences counts for both waiting periods.

f: 1362. What happens if the first waiting period ends while the second waiting period is incomplete?
b: She completes the remainder of the second waiting period.

f: 1363. What is Imam al-Shafi'i's view regarding overlapping waiting periods?
b: He says they do not overlap because the purpose is worship, requiring abstention from marriage and leaving the home.

f: 1364. What analogy does Imam al-Shafi'i use to argue that waiting periods do not overlap?
b: He compares them to two fasts occurring on the same day.

f: 1365. What is the Hanafi evidence for overlapping waiting periods?
b: The purpose of the waiting period is establishing that the womb is empty, and this has already been achieved through one waiting period.

f: 1366. According to the Hanafi school, what is the role of the worship aspect of the waiting period?
b: It is secondary, as shown by the fact that the waiting period ends even if she does not know it or consciously observe its restrictions.

f: 1367. How does a widow observing waiting period after death observe another waiting period after intercourse due to mistaken assumption?
b: She observes her waiting period by months while counting any menstruation she experiences during it.

f: 1368. Why does a widow count menstruations during the waiting period after mistaken intercourse?
b: To achieve overlap as much as possible.

f: 1369. When does the waiting period after divorce begin?
b: It begins immediately after the divorce occurs.

f: 1370. When does the waiting period after the husband's death begin?
b: It begins immediately after death.

f: 1371. If a woman does not know about the divorce or death until after the entire waiting period has passed, has her waiting period ended?
b: Yes. Her waiting period has ended.

f: 1372. Why does the waiting period begin from the time of divorce or death rather than when she learns of it?
b: Because the cause requiring the waiting period is the divorce or death, so the beginning is counted from when the cause occurred.

f: 1373. What fatwa do Hanafi scholars give regarding the beginning of waiting periods after divorce?
b: They issue fatwa that it begins from the time of acknowledgement to prevent suspicion of collusion.

f: 1374. When does the waiting period in an invalid marriage (nikāḥ fāsid) begin?
b: It begins after separation or after the man decides to stop intercourse with her.

f: 1375. What is Imam Zayd ibn Ali's view regarding the beginning of the waiting period in an invalid marriage?
b: He says it begins from the final intercourse because intercourse is the cause requiring the waiting period.

f: 1376. What is the Hanafi response to Imam Zayd ibn Ali's view?
b: Every intercourse occurring within an invalid marriage is treated as one intercourse because all of it is based on one contract.

f: 1377. Why is the waiting period not established before separation or the decision to abandon her in an invalid marriage?
b: Because another intercourse may still occur.

f: 1378. Why is intercourse under a doubtful basis treated like actual intercourse in legal rulings?
b: Because it is hidden and there is a need to know its legal consequences for others.

f: 1379. If a woman in waiting period says, "My waiting period has ended," and the husband denies it, whose statement is accepted?
b: Her statement is accepted along with her oath.

f: 1380. Why is the woman's statement accepted regarding the end of her waiting period?
b: Because she is entrusted regarding this matter, although she is accused of lying, so she takes an oath like someone entrusted with a deposit.

f: 1381. If a man gives his wife an irrevocable divorce, then marries her during her waiting period and divorces her before consummation of the second marriage, what does he owe?
b: He owes a complete dowry.

f: 1382. What happens to the woman's waiting period if she is divorced before consummation of the second marriage?
b: She must begin a new waiting period.

f: 1383. If a man divorces his wife with an irrevocable divorce, marries her during her waiting period, and divorces her before consummating the second marriage, what is the ruling according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: He owes a complete dowry and she must begin a new waiting period.

f: 1384. What is Muhammad's view regarding a man who divorces his wife before consummating the second marriage after remarrying her during the first waiting period?
b: He owes half the dowry, and she completes the first waiting period.

f: 1385. What is Muhammad's reasoning for requiring only half the dowry and completion of the first waiting period?
b: Because this is a divorce before consummation, so it does not require the full dowry or a new waiting period.

f: 1386. According to Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, why does the first waiting period continue after the second divorce?
b: Because the first divorce's effect was hidden due to the second marriage, and when the second marriage ends, the first ruling becomes apparent.

f: 1387. What is the Hanafi response to Muhammad's reasoning?
b: She was already in his possession due to the first consummation, and the effect of that possession — the waiting period — remained. The renewed marriage does not require a new possession.

f: 1388. What analogy do Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ use to explain why this is considered a divorce after consummation?
b: They compare it to someone who wrongfully possesses property and then purchases it; ownership occurs immediately through the contract without needing a new possession.

f: 1389. What is Imam Zayd ibn Ali's view regarding the waiting period in this case?
b: She has no waiting period at all.

f: 1390. Why does Imam Zayd ibn Ali say she has no waiting period?
b: Because the first waiting period ended when she remarried, and the second marriage does not require a waiting period because there was no consummation.

f: 1391. What is the ruling if a dhimmī husband divorces a dhimmī wife according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: There is no waiting period upon her.

f: 1392. What is the ruling if a Muslim woman from the land of war emigrates to Muslim lands according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: There is no waiting period upon her.

f: 1393. Can a Muslim woman who emigrates from the land of war marry immediately according to Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Yes, she may marry, except if she is pregnant.

f: 1394. What is the view of Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad regarding the waiting period of a dhimmī woman and an emigrant woman?
b: They say that the waiting period is required upon both of them.

f: 1395. What issue is the disagreement regarding a dhimmī woman's waiting period compared to?
b: It is similar to the disagreement regarding marriages among non-Muslims involving their own prohibited relatives.

f: 1396. When does Abu Hanifah's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ ruling regarding a dhimmī woman's waiting period apply?
b: When their religious belief is that she has no waiting period.

f: 1397. What is the reasoning of Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muhammad regarding an emigrant woman from the land of war?
b: If separation occurred through another cause, the waiting period would be obligatory; therefore, separation through difference of religion should also require it.

f: 1398. Why is the case different when the husband emigrates and leaves his wife behind?
b: Because the command to separate did not reach her.

f: 1399. What evidence does Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ use for allowing immediate marriage after emigration?
b: Allah's statement: “And there is no blame upon you if you marry them...” (Qur’an 60:10).

f: 1400. What is Abu Hanifah's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ reasoning regarding the purpose of the waiting period?
b: Wherever the waiting period is obligatory, it contains a right belonging to human beings.

f: 1401. Why does Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ not recognize the waiting period as a right in the case of someone from hostile lands?
b: Because such a person is treated as having no legal protection, to the extent that they could be taken as property.

f: 1402. Why is a pregnant emigrant woman from the land of war treated differently?
b: Because there is a child in her womb whose lineage is established.

f: 1403. What other narration is reported from Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding marrying a pregnant emigrant woman?
b: It is permissible to marry her but not to have intercourse with her, similar to a woman pregnant through fornication.

f: 1404. Which opinion regarding a pregnant emigrant woman is considered more correct?
b: The first opinion, that marriage and intercourse are both permissible, is considered more correct.

f: 1405. What is the ruling of mourning (ḥidād) for a permanently divorced woman and a woman whose husband has died?
b: The permanently divorced woman and the woman whose husband has died must observe mourning if they are adult Muslim women.

f: 1406. What is the evidence that a widow must observe mourning?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “It is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over a deceased person for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days.”

f: 1407. What is the position of al-Shāfiʿī regarding mourning for an irrevocably divorced woman?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said that she does not observe mourning, because mourning was legislated as sorrow over losing a husband who fulfilled his covenant until death, whereas a divorced woman has been harmed by separation rather than losing him through death.

f: 1408. What is the Hanafi evidence that an irrevocably divorced woman must observe mourning?
b: The evidence is the narration that the Prophet ﷺ prohibited the woman in waiting period from applying henna and said: “Henna is perfume.” Also, mourning is required due to losing the blessing of marriage, which protects and supports her. Irrevocable divorce cuts her off more severely than death because after separation she cannot even perform acts such as washing him after death.

f: 1409. What is the linguistic meaning and forms of the word ḥidād?
b: Mourning (al-ḥidād), also called al-iḥdād, are two linguistic forms referring to the same meaning.

f: 1410. What does mourning (ḥidād) require a woman to leave?
b: She must leave perfume, adornment, kohl, oil, perfumed items, and non-perfumed items used for beautification, except when there is an excuse.

f: 1411. What are the two reasons behind the prohibition of adornment during mourning?
b: 1. Displaying sorrow over the loss of marriage. 2. These things attract attention and beautify her, while she is prohibited from marriage during the waiting period, so avoiding them prevents a path toward something forbidden.

f: 1412. Why is kohl prohibited during mourning?
b: Because it has been authentically reported that the Prophet ﷺ did not permit the woman in mourning to use kohl.

f: 1413. Why is oil prohibited during mourning?
b: Oil contains a type of perfume and beautifies the hair, so it is prohibited just as it is prohibited for the person in iḥrām.

f: 1414. When is using oil permissible during mourning?
b: It is permissible due to necessity, such as using it as medicine rather than beautification. If she is accustomed to applying oil and fears harm without it, and this is apparent, it is permissible because what is normally expected is treated like what has actually occurred.

f: 1415. Is wearing silk clothing due to necessity permissible during mourning?
b: Yes, wearing silk due to a genuine necessity caused by an excuse is not problematic.

f: 1416. What is the ruling on applying henna during mourning?
b: She should not apply henna because of the evidence prohibiting beautification and perfume during mourning.

f: 1417. What is the ruling on wearing clothing dyed with safflower or saffron during mourning?
b: She should not wear such clothing because fragrance comes from these dyes.

f: 1418. Does a disbelieving woman have to observe mourning?
b: No, there is no mourning upon a disbelieving woman because she is not addressed by the rulings of the Sharīʿah.

f: 1419. Does a young girl have to observe mourning?
b: No, because legal responsibility has not been placed upon her.

f: 1420. Does a slave woman have to observe mourning?
b: Yes, the slave woman must observe mourning because she is addressed by the rights of Allah Most High in matters that do not cancel the rights of her master.

f: 1421. Why does a slave woman observe mourning but may not be restricted from leaving the house?
b: Mourning relates to the rights of Allah, whereas restricting her from leaving the house affects the rights of her master. The right of the servant (a human being) is given precedence due to his need.

f: 1422. Is mourning required during the waiting period of an Umm al-Walad?
b: No, there is no mourning in the waiting period of an Umm al-Walad because she has not lost the blessing of marriage in order to display sorrow over it, and the original ruling is permissibility.

f: 1423. Is mourning required during the waiting period of an invalid marriage (nikāḥ fāsid)?
b: No, there is no mourning in the waiting period of an invalid marriage because she has not lost the blessing of a valid marital relationship, and the original ruling is permissibility.

f: 1424. What is the ruling on directly proposing to a woman who is in her waiting period?
b: A woman in her waiting period should not be directly proposed to.

f: 1425. What type of proposal is permissible during the waiting period?
b: Indirect hints in proposing are permissible.

f: 1426. What is the evidence for allowing indirect proposals during the waiting period?
b: Allah Most High said: “And there is no blame upon you regarding what you indirectly propose of marriage to women... but do not make secret promises to them, except to speak words that are recognised as proper.” (al-Baqarah 2:235)

f: 1427. What did the Prophet ﷺ say regarding secret proposals?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The secret means marriage.”

f: 1428. How did Ibn ʿAbbās رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا explain indirect proposal?
b: He said that indirect proposal is when a man says: “I intend to marry.”

f: 1429. How did Saʿīd ibn Jubayr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ explain “speak recognised words”?
b: He explained it as saying things such as: “Indeed, I desire you,” or “Indeed, I wish that we could come together.”

f: 1430. Can a woman in revocable divorce leave her house during her waiting period?
b: No, a woman in revocable divorce may not leave her house during the day or night.

f: 1431. Can an irrevocably divorced woman leave her house during her waiting period?
b: No, an irrevocably divorced woman may not leave her house during the day or night.

f: 1432. Can a widow leave her house during her waiting period?
b: Yes, a widow may leave during the day and part of the night, but she may not spend the night outside her home.

f: 1433. What is the evidence that divorced women should remain in their homes during the waiting period?
b: Allah Most High said: “Do not remove them from their houses, nor should they leave, except that they commit an obvious immorality.” (al-Ṭalāq 65:1)

f: 1434. What are the two interpretations of “obvious immorality” in the verse regarding leaving the house?
b: It has been said that it refers to leaving the house itself, and it has also been said that it refers to adultery, in which case they leave so that the legal punishment can be carried out.

f: 1435. Why may a widow leave during the day while a divorced woman may not?
b: A widow has no maintenance due from her husband, so she needs to leave to seek her livelihood, and sometimes this may extend into the night. A divorced woman, however, continues to receive maintenance from her husband's wealth during her waiting period.

f: 1436. What is the ruling if a woman performs khulʿ in exchange for giving up her maintenance during the waiting period?
b: There are two views: it has been said that she may leave during the day, and it has been said that she may not leave because she surrendered her right.

f: 1437. Why is it possible for a woman who gave up her maintenance in khulʿ still to have permission to leave?
b: Because she only waived her own right, and that does not invalidate a remaining right owed to her.

f: 1438. Where must a woman observe her waiting period after divorce or the death of her husband?
b: She must observe it in the house which is attributed to her as her residence at the time of the separation or the death.

f: 1439. What is the evidence that a woman in waiting period must remain in her residence?
b: Allah Most High said: “Do not expel them from their houses.” (al-Ṭalāq 65:1)

f: 1440. What is meant by “their houses” in the verse?
b: It refers to the house attributed to her, meaning the house in which she resides.

f: 1441. If a woman was visiting her family and her husband divorces her, where does she observe her waiting period?
b: She must return to her residence and observe her waiting period there.

f: 1442. What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct the woman whose husband was killed regarding her residence?
b: He ﷺ said: “Remain in your house until the appointed term reaches its end.”

f: 1443. If a widow's share of her deceased husband's house is not enough for her and the heirs remove her from their share, may she move?
b: Yes, she may move because this is a move due to an excuse, and acts of worship are affected by excuses.

f: 1444. What other excuses allow a woman in waiting period to move from her residence?
b: She may move if she fears for her belongings, fears the house collapsing, or was living there through rent but cannot find the required payment.

f: 1445. What is the ruling if separation occurs through irrevocable divorce or three divorces while the couple remain in the same house?
b: There must be a barrier between them, and after that there is no harm.

f: 1446. Why must there be a barrier between a man and his irrevocably divorced wife during the waiting period?
b: Because he acknowledges the prohibition of being alone with her after irrevocable separation.

f: 1447. What happens if the woman fears harm from her divorced husband because he is immoral?
b: She may leave due to this excuse.

f: 1448. After moving away due to fear of harm, does the woman return to her original place?
b: No, she does not move away from the place to which she moved.

f: 1449. What is considered the better option when a divorced couple remain in the same house?
b: It is better that the husband leaves and allows her to remain in the house.

f: 1450. What is the ruling if a trustworthy woman is placed between them and can prevent contact?
b: This is good and removes the problem.

f: 1451. What happens if the house becomes too narrow for both of them?
b: She should leave, although it is better that he leaves.

f: 1452. If a woman travelled with her husband to Makkah and he divorces her three times or dies while they are away from their town, what does she do if the distance back is less than three days' travel?
b: She returns to her town because this is not considered beginning a new journey; rather, it is a continuation of the previous one.

f: 1453. If returning to her town is a journey of three days, what are her options?
b: She may either return or remain there, whether she has a guardian (maḥram) with her or not.

f: 1454. Why may she choose to remain if returning is a three-day journey?
b: Because remaining there may be more dangerous for her than leaving.

f: 1455. Which option is preferred if returning requires a three-day journey?
b: Returning is preferred so that she observes her waiting period in her husband's residence.

f: 1456. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, may a woman leave the town where she is observing waiting period before completing it if she has a maḥram?
b: No. She must remain until she completes her waiting period, then she may leave if she has a maḥram.

f: 1457. What is the position of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad regarding a woman leaving before completing her waiting period if she has a maḥram?
b: They said that if she has a maḥram with her, there is no harm in her leaving the town before completing her waiting period.

f: 1458. What is the evidence of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad for allowing her to leave with a maḥram?
b: Leaving removes the harm of being away from one's homeland and loneliness. This is an excuse, and the prohibition of travelling without a maḥram is removed when she has one.

f: 1459. What is the evidence of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ for preventing her from leaving before completing the waiting period?
b: The waiting period is a stronger restriction than the absence of a maḥram. A woman may leave for places less than the travel distance without a maḥram, but a woman in waiting period does not have this permission. Therefore, the restriction during waiting period is stronger.

f: 1460. What is the ruling if a man says: “If I marry so-and-so, she is divorced,” then marries her and she gives birth six months after the marriage?
b: The child’s lineage is established to him, and he owes her the dower.

f: 1461. Why is the child’s lineage established when she gives birth six months after marriage in this case?
b: Because she was his marital bed (firāsh). Since she gave birth after six months from the marriage, conception could have occurred before the conditional divorce while they were married.

f: 1462. How could conception have occurred before the conditional divorce in this case?
b: It is possible that he married her while having relations with her, and ejaculation coincided with the marriage contract.

f: 1463. Why is lineage established whenever possible?
b: Because lineage is treated with caution and is preserved whenever there is a possible explanation.

f: 1464. Why does the husband owe the dower when lineage is established?
b: Because establishing lineage from him legally indicates that intercourse occurred, and therefore the dower becomes confirmed.

f: 1465. When is the lineage of a child born to a woman divorced by revocable divorce established if she gives birth after two years or more?
b: Her child’s lineage is established unless she acknowledges that her waiting period has ended.

f: 1466. Why is lineage established after two years or more in a revocable divorce?
b: Because conception may have occurred during the waiting period, since her period of purity may be extended.

f: 1467. What happens if a woman divorced by revocable divorce gives birth before two years?
b: She becomes separated from her husband when her waiting period ends, and the child’s lineage is established.

f: 1468. Why is the husband not considered to have taken her back (performed rujuʿ) if she gives birth before two years after revocable divorce?
b: Because conception could have occurred either during marriage or during the waiting period. A revocation of marriage is not established through doubt.

f: 1469. What happens if a woman gives birth after more than two years following a revocable divorce?
b: She is considered to have been in a revocable divorce, and the husband is considered to have taken her back through intercourse.

f: 1470. Why is the husband considered to have taken her back if she gives birth after more than two years following revocable divorce?
b: Because conception occurred after the divorce, and the apparent assumption is that the child is his since she is not assumed to have committed adultery. Therefore, intercourse with her is treated as a revocation.

f: 1471. When is the lineage of a child born to a woman who was irrevocably divorced established?
b: Her child's lineage is established if she gives birth before two years from the time of separation.

f: 1472. Why is lineage established for an irrevocably divorced woman who gives birth before two years?
b: Because it is possible that the child was already present at the time of divorce. Therefore, it cannot be certain that the marital bond ended before conception.

f: 1473. What is the ruling if an irrevocably divorced woman gives birth exactly two years after separation?
b: The child’s lineage is not established.

f: 1474. Why is lineage not established if an irrevocably divorced woman gives birth exactly two years after separation?
b: Because conception occurred after divorce, and intercourse with her is prohibited, so the child cannot be attributed to him.

f: 1475. What is the exception if an irrevocably divorced woman gives birth exactly two years after separation?
b: If the husband claims the child, the child’s lineage is established.

f: 1476. How is it possible that an irrevocably divorced woman’s child born exactly two years later could belong to the husband?
b: It is possible that he had intercourse with her through a mistaken assumption (shubha) during the waiting period.

f: 1477. What is the ruling if an irrevocably divorced young woman, of an age where intercourse with someone like her is possible, gives birth after nine months?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ, lineage is not attributed to the husband unless she gives birth in less than nine months.

f: 1478. What is the position of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding the lineage of a child from a young woman in irrevocable divorce?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said that lineage is established from him up to two years.

f: 1479. Why does Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ establish lineage for a young woman in waiting period up to two years?
b: Because she is a woman in waiting period and it is possible that she was pregnant, and since she did not acknowledge the end of her waiting period, she resembles an adult woman.

f: 1480. What is the response of Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad to Abū Yūsuf’s رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ reasoning?
b: The end of her waiting period has a clear indication: the passing of the required months. When those months pass, the Sharīʿah judges that the waiting period has ended, and this is stronger than her own acknowledgement because the passage of time does not allow disagreement, whereas acknowledgement can be mistaken.

f: 1481. If a woman was divorced by revocable divorce, what is the ruling according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad?
b: The ruling is the same as in the case of irrevocable divorce: lineage is not established unless she gives birth within the required shorter period.

f: 1482. According to Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, until when is lineage established for a woman divorced by revocable divorce?
b: According to Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, lineage is established up to twenty-seven months.

f: 1483. How did Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ calculate the period of twenty-seven months for a revocably divorced woman?
b: He considered that the husband could have intercourse with her at the end of the three-month waiting period, and then she could give birth after the maximum pregnancy period of two years: 3 months + 24 months = 27 months.

f: 1484. What is the ruling if a young woman claims pregnancy during her waiting period?
b: The ruling regarding her is the same as the ruling regarding an adult woman because through her acknowledgement she is treated as having reached maturity.

f: 1485. When is the lineage of a child born to a woman whose husband has died established?
b: Her child's lineage is established if she gives birth between the time of his death and two years.

f: 1486. What is the position of Zayd ibn Thābit (reported from Zufar) regarding the lineage of a widow’s child born after the waiting period?
b: He said that if she gives birth after the widow’s waiting period has ended, and after six months, lineage is not established.

f: 1487. Why did Zayd ibn Thābit (Zufar) say that lineage is not established after the widow’s waiting period ends?
b: Because the Sharīʿah has ruled that her waiting period ends through the passing of the months, just as in the case of the young woman.

f: 1488. What is the response to Zayd ibn Thābit’s position regarding the widow?
b: The widow has another basis for ending her waiting period: giving birth. This differs from the young girl because the original assumption regarding her is that she cannot be pregnant, since she cannot conceive before puberty, creating doubt.

f: 1489. What happens if a woman in waiting period acknowledges that her waiting period ended and then gives birth within less than six months?
b: The child’s lineage is established because her falsehood becomes certain, so her acknowledgement is disregarded.

f: 1490. Why is the woman’s acknowledgement of the end of her waiting period ignored if she gives birth within less than six months afterward?
b: Because the birth proves that she was still pregnant during the waiting period, making her previous acknowledgement incorrect.

f: 1491. What happens if a woman gives birth after six months following her acknowledgement that her waiting period ended?
b: The child’s lineage is not established.

f: 1492. Why is lineage not established if she gives birth after six months following her acknowledgement?
b: Because it is possible that the pregnancy occurred after her acknowledgement, so her acknowledgement is not proven false.

f: 1493. To whom does the general wording of this ruling apply?
b: The wording applies generally to every woman observing a waiting period.

f: 1494. What is the ruling according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding establishing the lineage of a child born to a woman in a waiting period, and what testimony is required?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the lineage of a child born to a woman observing a waiting period is not established unless two men, or one man and two women, testify to the birth. However, if there is an obvious pregnancy or the husband has already acknowledged the pregnancy, lineage is established without requiring testimony.

f: 1495. Why do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ consider the testimony of one woman sufficient to establish the birth of a child during a waiting period?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ argue that the marital bond (firāsh) remains during the waiting period, and this establishes lineage. The only matter requiring proof is the occurrence of childbirth, which can be established by one woman's testimony because women are specifically relied upon in matters that men cannot observe.

f: 1496. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ not accept the testimony of only one woman for establishing lineage after birth during a waiting period?
b: Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ argues that the waiting period ends through the woman's acknowledgment of giving birth, and something that has ended cannot serve as proof. Therefore, lineage must be newly established through complete legal proof. This differs from cases where pregnancy was already apparent or the husband had acknowledged it, because lineage was already established before birth.

f: 1497. If a woman whose husband died gives birth during her waiting period, and the heirs confirm the birth without formal testimony, is the child's lineage established?
b: Yes, the child's lineage is established according to all scholars. This is because the heirs' confirmation is accepted regarding inheritance, since inheritance is their right. If they are legally qualified witnesses, their confirmation also establishes lineage regarding others.

f: 1498. If a woman marries a man and gives birth less than six months after the marriage, is the child attributed to the husband?
b: No, the child's lineage is not established from the husband because conception occurred before the marriage, so the child cannot be attributed to him.

f: 1499. If a woman gives birth six months or more after marriage, is the child's lineage established from the husband?
b: Yes, the child's lineage is established from the husband whether he acknowledges the child or remains silent, because the marital bond remains and the minimum pregnancy period has been fulfilled.

f: 1500. If a husband denies that his wife gave birth, how can the birth be legally established?
b: The birth is established through the testimony of one woman who testifies that she witnessed the childbirth, because childbirth is among the matters where women's testimony is accepted.

f: 1501. If a husband denies the lineage of a child born from his wife while they are married, does he perform liʿān?
b: Yes, he performs liʿān because lineage is established through the marital bond (firāsh), while his denial constitutes an accusation. The existence of a child is not a condition for liʿān, because liʿān may occur even when there is no child.

f: 1502. If a husband and wife disagree after childbirth, with the husband claiming he married her four months ago and the wife claiming she was married six months ago, whose statement is accepted?
b: The wife's statement is accepted and the child is attributed to the husband because the apparent situation supports her claim. Giving birth indicates that the pregnancy occurred within a valid marriage rather than through fornication.

f: 1503. If a man says to his wife, "If you give birth to a child, then you are divorced," and one woman testifies that she gave birth, does divorce occur according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, divorce does not occur because the condition for divorce has not been established through complete legal proof. One woman's testimony is accepted only for proving childbirth itself, not for establishing the resulting divorce.

f: 1504. If a man makes divorce conditional upon childbirth and one woman testifies to the birth, what is the position of Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ?
b: Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ say that divorce occurs because one woman's testimony is accepted regarding childbirth, and the divorce depends upon the occurrence of childbirth. Therefore, her testimony is accepted for the consequence as well.

f: 1505. What evidence do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ use for accepting one woman's testimony in matters connected to childbirth?
b: They rely on the statement of the Prophet ﷺ: "The testimony of women is accepted in matters which men are unable to see." Since childbirth is established through one woman's testimony, they argue that the legal consequences resulting from childbirth should also be established through it.

f: 1506. What is Abū Ḥanīfah's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ response to the argument that one woman's testimony should establish divorce after childbirth?
b: Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ responds that the woman is claiming the occurrence of the condition (ḥinth), and conditions leading to divorce require complete proof. The acceptance of women's testimony is only due to necessity regarding childbirth itself, and that necessity does not extend to divorce because divorce is a separate ruling.

f: 1507. If a husband has already acknowledged his wife's pregnancy, is testimony required for her to become divorced when childbirth occurs according to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, she becomes divorced without requiring testimony because his acknowledgment of the pregnancy is an acknowledgment of what necessarily follows from it, namely childbirth. Since he has already accepted her trustworthiness, her statement is accepted like the statement of a person entrusted with returning a trust.

f: 1508. Why do Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Muḥammad رَحِمَهُمَا اللَّهُ require the testimony of a midwife even if the husband has acknowledged the pregnancy?
b: They argue that proof is still required for the occurrence of the condition leading to divorce. Since her claim is that childbirth occurred, testimony is required, and the testimony of the midwife serves as proof for this matter.

f: 1509. What is the maximum duration of pregnancy according to the Hanafi position?
b: According to the Hanafi position, the maximum duration of pregnancy is two years. This is based on the statement of ʿĀ’ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: "A child does not remain in the womb for more than two years, even if a spindle were to break."

f: 1510. What is the minimum duration of pregnancy according to the Hanafi scholars?
b: The minimum duration of pregnancy is six months. This is derived from the verses: "His carrying and his weaning are thirty months" (Qur'an 46:15) and "His weaning is in two years" (Qur'an 31:14). Since weaning takes two years, six months remain for pregnancy.

f: 1511. What is the position of al-Shāfiʿī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding the maximum duration of pregnancy?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ holds that the maximum duration of pregnancy is four years. The Hanafi scholars reject this based on the narration from ʿĀ’ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, which they consider to be based on transmitted knowledge rather than personal reasoning.

f: 1512. If a man marries a slave woman, divorces her, and later purchases her, what is the ruling if she gives birth less than six months after he purchased her?
b: The child is attributed to him because she is treated as a woman observing a waiting period, and conception may have occurred before the purchase while she was still married to him.

f: 1513. If a man marries a slave woman, divorces her, purchases her, and she gives birth six months or more after the purchase, is the child attributed to him?
b: No, the child is not attributed to him. She is treated as a slave woman, and a new event is attributed to the nearest possible time. Therefore, a claim of lineage is required.

f: 1514. Does the ruling regarding lineage after purchasing a divorced slave woman apply to all types of divorce?
b: Yes, it applies to irrevocable divorce, khulʿ, and revocable divorce. However, if she was divorced with two divorces, lineage is established up to two years from the time of divorce because she became permanently prohibited and conception cannot be attributed after divorce since purchase does not make her lawful to him again.

f: 1515. If a man says to his slave woman, "If there is a child in your womb, then he is from me," and one woman testifies to the birth, what is the ruling?
b: The child becomes his slave woman's child. The purpose is to establish the identity of the child, and this is established through the testimony of the midwife according to unanimous agreement.

f: 1516. If a man says, "The boy is my son," then dies, and the boy's mother claims, "I am his wife," what is the ruling according to istiḥsān?
b: According to juristic preference (istiḥsān), she is considered his wife, the boy is considered his son, and both inherit from him.
